findings.file: tests/test_merge_manifest.py (rw4); tests/test__evidence_io.py (pa4, uw1); the code each exercises on Windows
findings.issue: The plan-writers commit is red on Windows in CI (run 44578935890 on eba49be5, jobs 'selftests (windows, plain 1)' and '(windows, plain 2)'; every other job green; read it with gh run view 44578935890 --json jobs). Three cases: rw4, the resolver's allow case with no stray write (exit 0 and the renumbering are as expected in its printed output, so the failing conjunct is the files' spelling or the no-marker check, on a platform where git may check text out with other line endings; rw4b beside it passes); pa4, close-phase's merge stamp keeping a record landed as it asks for the lock (first conjunct False: the landed record is not kept, or the landing did not land it, on Windows); uw1, the unwritable lock directory, which reports COULD NOT RUN HERE because a directory's mode does not stop a write on Windows and is counted as a failure. The first two may be product behaviour on Windows (a write lost, or bytes compared across a line-ending conversion: the resolver's new comparison is the likeliest place), not only test shape.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.26-6l3 (f7909a033881): Each is settled by what the Windows runner shows, through a CI run on a disposable branch: the failing conjunct named, then either the product fixed (a comparison that survives git's line-ending conversion; the record kept) with the case green on Windows, or the case made to state a Windows-shaped precondition it cannot stage the way the suite's other platform-shaped cases do, never counted as a pass it did not earn.

findings.issue: Regression of the malformed-records change, found by an independent review of its uncommitted tree: `run-test-gate.py --reconcile` replaces a task's malformed RED record with an OLDER GREEN ledger run. The reader now leaves the malformed record out, so the subject's newest run is the older row, and the held record reads as absent and is replaced. Output says `moved: task ... -> <older run>` beside an UNREAD line saying no record of the file was reconciled, which is then false. After it the plan holds the green run as lastRun and testEvidence, the unreadable line is gone, `audit-status --gate --fail-on failing-tests` goes from failed to passed, and the commit binding would bind to the older run. Before the change the same fixture raised and wrote nothing. No case covers reconcile over a malformed record; the phase scope was not probed and is likely the same.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.27-6l3 (c4ff8c71d443): A subject whose own record could not be read is never answered from an older run, by anything that picks a subject's newest run: one function in the evidence module answers newest-or-unreadable for a subject and every picker goes through it (reconcile refuses the subject and leaves its record's bytes; the binding already does this). Cases red at the head through the real command, task and phase scope, asserting the shard's bytes, the gate condition and the output.

findings.issue: Same class as the reconcile regression: `audit-lookup.py run latest --task <id>` over a plan whose newest record of that task is malformed prints the older green run as the answer, exit 0, with no word about the record; `run <id of the malformed run>` says no such run is recorded. The lookup is handed the ledger's unreadable count only, while its own docstring promises the miss says when the run may sit in what could not be read.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.27-6l3 (c4ff8c71d443): The lookup goes through the same newest-or-unreadable answer: `latest` refuses or qualifies when the subject's own record is unreadable, and a miss names the plan records that could not be read.

findings.issue: Older than this change, and the reviewer rated it high by the rule that a plan holding a provisional phase must never read as nothing held; recorded as med because it needs a hand edit or a broken writer, and somebody who can edit the plan by hand can remove the bug or the phase outright. With a merged provisional phase in the plan, each of these lets a tag command through silently: the index's `phases` not a list; a phase entry not an object; `meta` not an object; `meta.fullGate` present with a wrong type or blank entries (read as no third place declared); a bug entry not an object (skipped); `mergedAt` falsy while `mergedHead` is recorded; a duplicated key whose later value is null. The guard's own rule and SECURITY.md's table say a plan that cannot be read is a deny.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.27-6l3 (c4ff8c71d443): The guard refuses, naming the problem, when the structure it decides from is not the shape it reads: phases, a phase entry, a bug entry, meta, a present fullGate that is not a list of non-blank strings; a recorded merge head with no usable merge moment reads as unknown, not unmerged; a duplicated key in a plan file is refused by the loader the guard uses. Allow cases stay green on a well-formed plan and on a plan with no fullGate key. This is plan reading, not command reading; a refused edit to the guard goes to the owner verbatim.

findings.issue: A record that names `status`, `runId`, `at` or `testedState` in `sharedWithRepeated` passes the shape check, and the reader then takes that field from the carried run, over the record's own value: a failed record reads as passed, sharing `runId` makes the red run vanish, sharing `at` backdates it; the binding's own sentence called the red run's verdict passed. The writer never shares these, so only a hand edit reaches it, but the changelog and guide now say a moment or identity written into a record by hand never names another subject.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.27-6l3 (c4ff8c71d443): A shared path whose top key the writer never shares is a problem of the record (unreadable, named), and so is a shared path the record also holds; the schema says the same where it can; a case per never-shared key through the binding.

findings.issue: With fd 1 closed at exec the hook's stdout is None, the write raises an error `_deny` does not catch, and the hook exits 1 with a traceback, which does not block; its docstring promises exit 2 when stdout cannot take the reason. (A closed pipe does give exit 2.) Separately the bypass's arming message catches Exception only, so a SystemExit in the guard's reading still crashes it.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.27-6l3 (c4ff8c71d443): `_deny` returns 2 on any failure to write, the stderr write guarded too; a case with stdout closed at exec. The arming message catches what the guard's entry point catches.

findings.issue: The reader checks a carried run and each kept base run as a run record, the published schema leaves both untyped, so the validator calls a plan valid that every reader refuses a record of, and the new comment saying the two never disagree is untrue for those keys. Separately the validator's phase-gate suite-gap warning reads the ledger's unreadable count only: when the one record naming a suite is unreadable it warns that the phase gate runs no suite and says nothing about the record. And when a record matches both arms of the `oneOf` the message names no field to repair.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.27-6l3 (c4ff8c71d443): The schema types both as a run record (a warning in 3.x); the validator's gap warning says the gap is not established while a plan record could not be read, the way it treats an unreadable ledger; the both-arms message names `steps` and the share.

findings.issue: SECURITY.md was left out of the malformed-records change on purpose and now has sentences that are untrue or missing: its table row that a manifest that cannot be read is a deny (untrue for the structural shapes), that each list is read and reported on its own (a decision that raises is now one refusal naming neither), and nothing states that an error while deciding is a deny or what a closed stdout does. The changelog and guide say recording the gate again replaces a malformed record and do not say reconcile touched it too.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.27-6l3 (c4ff8c71d443): Each sentence made true against the guard as it stands after the repairs above, quoted before and after in the hand-back.

findings.file: plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_evidence_io.py (reusable_run); plugins/audit/scripts/governance/run-test-gate.py (its two call sites); the remedy sentence every unreadable-record refusal prints
findings.issue: Second recurrence of one class (a reader answers from an older run when the subject's own record cannot be read), found by the independent review of the task that was meant to close the class with one function: the gate's reuse lookup is a picker that function does not reach. With a subject's newest red held only as its malformed plan record and an older green in the ledger for the same content, `run-test-gate.py <plan> <phase>` prints GATE GREEN, verdict reused from the older run, no check ran; with --record it writes that green as the subject's new record and the binding then binds passed. The refusals this phase added (reconcile, doctor, binding, status, lookup) all tell the person to re-record the subject's gate, which is exactly that command; only --record --no-reuse measures. The red is held only in the plan whenever ledger writes are off, which the phase's last task makes the default, so this becomes the ordinary path. The same behaviour is at the previous commit; it is not a regression of the task reviewed.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.28-6l3 (5e2506f4801f): The property is held where rows are produced, not by a list of pickers: after a read, a subject whose own record cannot be read has no row any reader can take as its verdict or repeat, and the read says so in one place every reader already looks. The reuse lookup measures for such a subject, the remedy sentence names a command that measures, and one black-box case runs every command that prints or decides from runs over the fixture family and fails when the older run is given as the subject's answer.

findings.issue: Same class, third instance: a group member whose own phase record is a malformed red newer than the carrier's green run lands. The carrier binds, `member_red` is handed the records without the lost ones and returns nothing, so the landing goes over the member's own newer red. The executor of the one-function task listed this picker as owed, not safe; the previous commit behaves the same.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.28-6l3 (5e2506f4801f): Closed by the same source-level property; a case through the real landing with a member whose record is unreadable: refused, naming the record.

findings.issue: `member_red` still selects a member's rows the old way, so a kept base run (a measurement of the base commit, not of the member) newer than the carrier's run refuses the landing as the member's own failed verdict, while the binding, corrected in the task reviewed, says the member has no verdict. The two disagree about one phase and the person is pushed to override.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.28-6l3 (5e2506f4801f): One selection of a subject's own runs, used by the binding and by the member check; a case where they are asked about the same phase and must agree.

findings.issue: A task whose gate falls back to its phase's writes its run onto the PHASE's record, and reading the record back drops the task id because identity comes from where a record sits. Held only as a record, that run is the phase's: a task's green binds the phase over the phase's older red (with the ledger row present the phase is refused), and the task's red is invisible to the task's own binding, which binds an older green. The new comment and guide sentence saying such a run is the task's and never the phase's are true of ledger rows only. Related: re-recording such a task prints that the task's pointer now names the run while the task's own malformed record stays, so reconcile keeps failing until a hand repair. Older than the task reviewed; it matters once ledger writes are off.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.28-6l3 (5e2506f4801f): A run is held by the subject it measured: either the task's record takes it, or the phase's record keeps who ran it and the reader gives it back; the comment and the guide say what is true; cases with the ledger row absent, both directions.

findings.issue: The derived pickers case counts a function as going through the one answer when it calls it and ignores the result, does not derive pickers built on the newest-row helper (the reuse lookup is one), and does not scan tools. The guide says one function is asked by every reader of a subject's newest run and the changelog says the phase's own run decides now; neither is true of the reuse lookup, the member check or the report's evidence cell. SECURITY.md says a fullGate entry that is not a key name makes the list unknown (the code refuses only non-strings and blanks) and states the unplaced-merge refusal without its condition (it applies only when a runnable fullGate exists).
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.28-6l3 (5e2506f4801f): The case is replaced or joined by the black-box one; each sentence made true, quoted before and after.

findings.issue: Residues of the guard's structure reading. A plan with no `bugs` key is refused though the schema makes the key optional (the plugin's own verbs always write it; unchanged from before). A merged phase whose id is null is skipped, so the guard allows (hand edit only; the validator refuses it). The structure is parsed once per list, about 46 ms each over this repository's plan as profiled by the reviewer (cProfile of the hook's decision over a copy of the plan), which is the whole of the slowdown the executor measured on publishing commands; it grows with the bytes of the shards. And the older cost: the reviewer measured the phase list at 4.7 s for 350 merged phases on a fixture with a full gate declared, against the hook's 10 s timeout; what Claude Code does with a publishing command when this hook times out is not verified, and if it lets the command run the guard fails open at that size.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.28-6l3 (5e2506f4801f): The plan is parsed once per decision; a null phase id is a structure problem; an absent bugs key is either read as no bugs with the reason stated or kept as a refusal with the reason stated; the timeout behaviour is looked up in Claude Code's documentation and SECURITY.md says what it is, with the size at which the guard would meet it and the command that measures.

findings.file: plugins/audit/scripts/report/render-report.py and the report's page renderer (evidence cell)

findings.file: tools/check-browser-install.py:_builtin_call_problem (the `eval` branch, ~line 1253 of the working tree), and the docstring sentence 'a builtin on BUILTINS called in the one shape its row allows' / BUILTINS row for eval 'the reader holds it to that stub's output'
findings.issue: contradicts task clause 1 ('NOTHING the action's shell starts may be anything but a stub or an allow-listed tool'; hold it as a positive rule): the `eval` shape check accepts a double-quoted word that starts with `"$(`, ends with `)"`, has exactly one substitution and that substitution is `apt-config`, but it never checks the characters between. So `v='; ../../../../../../../../bin/echo ESCAPED #'` followed by `eval "$(apt-config shell s D/d)$v)"` has script_problems() == [] (I ran script_problems on that text with the module imported, no writes: it returned []), and the same text under plain bash started the real /bin/echo through a relative path (output ESCAPED). The reader reads the single-quoted assignment as a literal, the prelude disables no program started by a slash path and sd7 sees no absolute path, so both halves are passed and the docstring's claim that eval is held to the stub's output is false. bp10 only has `eval "$x"`, which is why the row stays green.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.29-6l3 (7411b3676bcb): Hold eval to the exact word, not to its first and last characters: accept only a text that matches a fixed shape such as `^"\$\(apt-config [A-Za-z:/ ]+\)"$` (nothing between the substitution and the quotes, no `$`, backslash or quote inside), or have _word record that a dq word is one substitution and nothing else. Add bp10 rows for `eval "$(apt-config shell s D/d)$v)"` and `eval "$(apt-config x) ; y"`, and a bx row that appends the variable-assignment plus eval pair with the file outside, refused by the reader.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause 1: the printf rule is `args[0]["quoted"] == "sq"`, 'so it is never `-v`' (BUILTINS row, docstring). Quote removal happens before the builtin sees its arguments, so `printf '-v' 'a[$(../../../../../../../../usr/bin/touch x)]' y` has script_problems() == [] (ran it, no writes) while bash parses `'-v'` as the option. The subscript is single-quoted so the reader never reads the substitution it carries; on a bash that evaluates a printf -v subscript (the case bx13 was written for) that starts a real tool by a relative path. I did not run it on a bash 5; this finding rests on the reader accepting it, and on the executor's own reason for refusing `printf -v`. bx13 proves only the unquoted spelling.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.29-6l3 (7411b3676bcb): Require the format's decoded text, not its quoting, to be safe: accept printf only when args[0] is single-quoted AND its text does not start with `'-` (or require it to contain a `%` conversion and no leading dash), and add a bp10 row `printf '-v' x y` and a bx13 twin with the option quoted.

findings.file: tools/check-browser-install.py (docstring 'WHAT A STEP CAN START', 'What stays outside that')
findings.issue: The 'stays outside' list is stated as complete ('each item is one neither half closes') but findings 1 and 2 are two further shapes the reader accepts that bash reads otherwise; the first item ('a shape it accepts that bash reads otherwise is not seen') covers the class in general only, while the same docstring says the builtins are held 'in the one shape its row allows'. Once 1 and 2 are fixed the same over-claim remains for `[` and `set --`, which were checked by reading only.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.29-6l3 (7411b3676bcb): After fixing 1 and 2, re-read each remaining row of _builtin_call_problem for the same question (does the check look at the decoded argument, or at its first and last character), and say in the docstring which rows are held by exact match and which by shape.

findings.issue: Case bk11 (the command hash written through BASH_CMDS, run past the reader) has never been seen red on any bash. On bash 3.2 the variable does not exist. On bash 5 (CI run 44673626435, a disposable probe with the prelude's disabling loop removed, the environment left writable, enable left on and BASH_CMDS left writable) every other construction case went red, bk1 to bk10 and bk12, and bk11 still passed with exit 2. So either the prelude's unset of BASH_CMDS is what holds it (bash drops a special variable's properties when it is unset) and the read-only line adds nothing for it, or the case fails for a reason of its own and asserts nothing about the hold.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.29-6l3 (7411b3676bcb): Show bk11 red on bash 5 by taking away the thing that holds it (a probe with the unset removed as well), and say in the prelude which line is the hold; if it cannot be made red, the case is restated as what it does show or removed, and the docstring stops naming the construction as a hold for that escape.

findings.file: plugins/audit/scripts/git/close-phase.py (the read of the plan's records at the branch tip)
findings.issue: Given a relative plan path and a project directory spelled through a symlink, close-phase says the plan is outside the repository, reads no records at the branch tip, adds a gate note and lands: a phase whose record at the tip is failed, or cannot be read, closes with exit 0, bound to an older green. With an absolute path, or the real directory, the same close refuses.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.28-6l3 (5e2506f4801f): The two paths are compared as real paths, and a close that cannot read the plan's records at the branch tip refuses with the reason instead of adding a note; a case drives the symlinked spelling over a red and over an unreadable record.

findings.issue: A run record whose `at` names no moment (an empty string, text that is not a time, a date that does not exist) passes the record check and the validator, is ordered as the oldest, and so the subject's older green run answers as its newest: the gate prints a verdict reused from the older green and records a passed repeat over the red, a task then closes bound to it, and a member's red does not stop its landing.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.28-6l3 (5e2506f4801f): A record whose moment cannot be placed is an unreadable record like any other: it becomes the subject's newest row, the older runs are withheld, the validator names the file and the field, and the black-box case carries this shape for every entry point.

findings.issue: A run record holding the same key twice reads as its last value: a record with `status` failed and then `status` passed is read as passed, the gate reuses it as green, and the validator and the doctor report nothing. The release guard already refuses a plan with a duplicate key; the plugin's own readers do not see one. A merge hunk resolved as keep-both produces exactly this record.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.28-6l3 (5e2506f4801f): The plan's files are read with a duplicate-key check where run records are read, and a record holding a duplicate key is an unreadable record; the validator names it.

findings.issue: The plan merge treats a run record as an object to merge field by field. With a red on the base, one side recording a green and the other a newer red, the conflicts are the run id, the duration and the moment only; resolving each to one side leaves that side's run id with the other side's status: a run that was red is read back as passed. With the ledger off the record is the only account of the run, so nothing contradicts it.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.30-6l3 (fb4c3bfd9281): A run record and the pointer beside it merge as one value: both sides changed it means one conflict on the whole record, resolved to one side whole, never a mix of fields; a case builds the three-sided shape and shows no resolution yields a record neither side wrote.

findings.issue: A phase measured green whose own run record is then made unreadable (a status written twice, a moment that is no moment, steps that are not a list) still reads `tests passed` in the status render, beside the render's own banner that run records cannot be read, and `audit-status --gate`, with the default conditions and with `--fail-on failing-tests`, exits 0 with GATE PASSED: the condition and the word read the pointer, not the record. The validator and the doctor warn and exit 0. So a CI gate on the plan's state stays green over a record nobody can read; only a close and a task's done refuse.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.31-6l3 (d2f6e199ea9e): A subject whose own newest record cannot be read gets no passing word in any render, and `failing-tests` trips on it with a sentence naming the record and the remedy; the JSON payload carries the same state; a case holds the three shapes for a task and a phase, and the allow direction (a readable green) stays quiet.

findings.issue: After a task's gate source changes, an older green measured on the task's own gate is reused over a newer red of the same task measured on the phase's gate: the reuse lookup requires the row's scope to equal the caller's, so the newer run of the same holder is never weighed. Seen with the ledger on at the branch head and in the reworked tree; with the ledger off the head reused too.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.28-6l3 (5e2506f4801f): The newest run of the holder decides whether anything may be reused: a newer run of the same holder that is not the reused one, on either gate, stops the reuse and the gate measures; a case drives the flip in both ledger states.

findings.file: plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/_manifest_io.py (read_json, save_plan_json) and every verb that saves a plan file through it
findings.issue: A plan file that writes a key twice (the shape a keep-both merge resolution leaves) is parsed with the last copy winning and saved back with one copy, silently, by every verb that writes the plan (`audit-task.py note`, `done`, and the others that go through `read_json`/`save_plan_json`). With a task holding its newest red record and then a second copy of the key carrying an older green, an unrelated `note` rewrites the shard with the green alone; from then the lookup names the green, the gate reuses it and `done` closes bound to it, ledger on and off. The run-record reader refuses the shape now, and the one writer that asks it refuses too, but any other save destroys the evidence first.
findings.resolution: The plan is parsed through one door that notices a key written twice anywhere in a plan file, and no verb saves a file it read that way: it refuses with the file, the path of the key and the hand step that gets out. Every reader that answers from the plan either goes through that door or is named with why it cannot.

findings.issue: A phase that writes its `tasks` key twice (one copy holding a task with its newest red record, the second the same task with an older green) is read from the last copy by every reader, silently: the lookup names the green, the gate reuses it, the validator says nothing, `done` closes bound to the green and rewrites the shard without the first copy. A container's duplicate is asked only of an object that itself holds a record.
findings.resolution: A key written twice on any object that holds records below it (`tasks`, `phases`, the index's phase list) makes every record under it unreadable and is named by the validator; the one-file and the sharded layouts both.

findings.issue: When the gate entry that names the task's tests.add file is a shell command joined with '&&', the brief's submit block writes it unquoted after '--'. The shell then splits it: submit's red-first helper is handed only the first command, and the rest runs as a separate command with the return's heredoc attached to it. An executor copying the block as printed files a return whose red-first proof ran the wrong command.
findings.resolution: The block hands the helper one argv the shell cannot split (the gate entry quoted as one 'sh -c' word, or the helper given the entry by name), and a case renders a brief for a task whose gate holds '&&' and runs the block it prints against a stub submit.

findings.file: plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_runner_output.py (_house_tally) and the red-first helper submit runs
findings.issue: The red-first helper grades its command's output by one house tally, the last 'N/M cases passed' line, so a command that runs two suites is graded by the second suite's counts alone; an executor whose tests.add entries live in two suites must file with one and leave the other suite's entries 'not checked'. In the same filing six cases the suite prints on the tree (bb-table, bb-drive-sites, bb-fixture, bb-remedy, bb-panel-state, bb-cost) were reported as not printed by the submit's own run; why was not established.
findings.resolution: The helper reads each suite's tally and each case label in a combined output (or takes one command per tests.add file), and the bb-* gap is explained by running the submit's red command by hand at the head and in the tree and comparing what each prints.

findings.file: CHANGELOG.md:70-73; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (the _units paragraph, 'a start beside a re-recorded red-first proof is two clean merges'); tests/test__manifest_merge.py wv27 (third 'apart' shape)
findings.issue: The shipped prose says a task's start beside a re-recorded red-first proof merges clean. It does so only when the start moves no status (a retry that bumps attempts and startedAt). A start in the ordinary sense moves status pending to in_progress, and then _units joins the close row (it shares `status`) because both sides changed it: I ran merge3 read-only on base pending, ours {status:in_progress, startedAt, attempts:1}, theirs {redFirst:{status:proved}} and it returned ONE conflict, tasks[P7.1].{status,startedAt,attempts,redFirst}. wv27 and the docs use a fixture whose status stays in_progress on all three sides, so the case never shows the plain start the sentence names. The behaviour is conservative (a conflict, never a mixed record), so this is a false claim in CHANGELOG, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE and layout-adjacent prose, not a data hazard.
findings.resolution: Either narrow the sentence to 'a retry that moves no status' in CHANGELOG.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md and add a wv27 fixture with a start that moves status expecting one conflict, or change the rows so a start does not pull in the close row through `status` alone.

The task's recorded gate run (repeatedRun.durationMs 273991, 'machine to itself') took about 274 s for the four gate files; the red-first helper's fixed-tree run was still going at 114 s; sweep-costs.json holds 20.0 for test_merge_manifest.py and 0.2 for test__manifest_merge.py, and the sweep's DEFAULT_TIMEOUT floor is 300 s. rr1-rr10 build about eight real git repositories with the driver installed, and wv23/wv25 parse every .py under scripts/ and walk the schema about twenty times. tasks.title: The browser jobs' time bound is about the slice: the Chromium install is timed by step and cached, and each bound's basis is re-measured
tasks.description:
The `browser (report)` job is bounded at 19 minutes on a recorded longest run of about nine, and on three runs in one day it took 17m44s once and was cut at the bound twice, the second time with the slice's VERIFY OK printed in the same second. Two costs sit in that job and in `browser (panel)` beside it. The install step (`npm ci`, then `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`) took between six and nine minutes. The slice took over eleven where its recorded longest whole job was nine.

Measure before changing: split the install into steps that each print their own duration (the package install, the browser download, the system packages) and read one run. Then remove what can be removed: cache the browser download keyed by the pinned playwright version in the lock file, and install only the system packages the runner image lacks. A cache miss must still install and pass; a cache hit must not skip a version change. For the slice: read its per-step seconds from the run's log (verify.sh prints them) and compare with the run the `longest` line names; if a step grew, name it and the commit range in the outcome and file what you find rather than fixing a product regression inside this task.

Then re-record: each browser job's `longest` line names a run measured after this change, and its bound is two to three times that, which is the rule tools/gate-parity.py holds. Do not raise a bound to make room for a cost you did not measure.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. One dispatched run (the orchestrator dispatches it on the phase's CI branch; say in the outcome which lines to read) shows the install by step, and a second shows the cached path with its seconds.
2. `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` is green: every job's bound is backed by its `longest` line.
3. The outcome states the job's whole duration before and after, each with its run id, and what remains of the slice's growth.
4. Nothing in the slice itself is skipped, narrowed or moved to the release tier to buy time.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: tools/gate-parity.py's job bounds and its matrix rules, tools/verify.sh's slices (unchanged), CONTRIBUTING.md and CLAUDE.md where they describe CI's shape, and the release-tier jobs that share the install step.

gate: python3 tools/gate-parity.py
python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tools/gate-parity.py

outcome.technical: Only .github/workflows/ci.yml changed. (1) The single `npm ci && npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` step in browser (panel) and browser (report) is now seven steps, identical in both jobs: npm ci; read the playwright-core pin from package-lock.json and ImageOS/ImageVersion (exits 1 if any is missing); actions/cache@v6 on <home>/.cache/ms-playwright keyed by runner os/arch and the playwright-core version; `npx playwright install chromium`, run on a hit as well so a version change is never skipped; derive the packages `playwright install-deps --dry-run chromium` names that dpkg-query does not report installed (exits 1 if no install line or no package); actions/cache@v6 on <home>/.cache/chromium-sysdeps keyed by the image version and a hash of that list; then `apt-get update` plus `--download-only` only for a .deb the restored set lacks, followed by `dpkg -i` on the set. Only the packages the image lacks are named, so mesa is no longer upgraded. (2) Measured on head 55d48673. Run 44363694425 missed both caches: panel 17:53:48-17:59:19 = 5m31s, report 17:53:48-18:05:59 = 12m11s, install 21s and 26s, mirror fast ('Fetched 21.1 MB in 0s'/'in 1s'). Run 44366022835 hit both ('every package the image lacks is in the restored set; no archive is asked'): panel 18:06:27-18:12:04 = 5m37s, report 18:06:27-18:19:04 = 12m37s, install 12s and 15s. Before the change: report 17m44s (run 44341247041) and 17m57s (run 44270291891); runs 44318839994 and 44356971266 were cut at the bound; panel 11m36s (44341247041) and 14m49s (42283005055); install 3m25s to 9m05s in the four runs read today, nearly all of it the apt fetch (for example 32.1 MB in 8m11s at 65.4 kB/s, job 134852070227). (3) The `longest` lines now read browser-panel 5m37s and browser-report 12m37s (both run 44366022835, start and end given), and the PROVISIONAL marking is gone. The bounds are 16 (panel; allowed 11m14s-16m51s, set above the minimum to hold a slow miss) and 26 (report; minimum 25m14s). A comment says what a slow miss still costs: the fetch of the packages the image lacks, 19.1 MB in 9m22s at 34.0 kB/s in run 42283005055, about nine minutes added to either job. The two measured runs had a fast mirror, so they show no saving on a slow day; the comment says so. (4) The slice is unchanged and still the remaining pole. The report slice took 11m25s (miss) and 12m04s (hit), against 8m13s in run 41322244766, the run the old `longest` line named (its log is still readable). Growth there: interactive-check steps 1m00s -> 3m00s, one-status 47s -> 2m18s, live plan 6m18s -> 5m47s; checks per page about tripled (acme-store 200 -> 584). Source: tools/check-report-interactive.mjs, commits 03f4114d (P163.1) through 1d0e3673 (P165.5). Filed in the fault register by the orchestrator, not fixed here. The report job is now about 12.5 minutes against the ten-minute workflow budget; the panel is about 5.5. (5) The cache helps only within one branch, or across branches when main holds a saved entry. Main's push runs skip the browser jobs once a commit is verified, so main rarely saves one; seeding it is the owner's call. (6) Process note: in stage two three Edit calls were refused with 'File has not been read yet' (file state was lost on resume). A `sed -i` for the two timeout values had been sent in the same parallel batch, so it ran (30->16, 36->26); after re-reading the file, the comment edits were made with Edit. Checks: `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` exit 0; Ruby YAML parse; the shell blocks run against stubs (miss, hit, partial set, three refusals). Dependants: tools/gate-parity.py unchanged and still correct (its bound rule holds the new lines; no job added or renamed, so the matrix and job-cap rules are unaffected); tools/verify.sh slices unchanged; CONTRIBUTING.md unchanged and still correct (every job is still setup plus one verify.sh --only call); CLAUDE.md not edited and still correct for the same reason; no release-tier job shares the install (resample has none, lint's npm ci is untouched). The pgo7 failures in both probe runs are tests/test_run_test_gate.py, a separate fault, not caused by this change.
outcome.descriptive: The browser jobs' install drops from 3-9 minutes to 12-26 seconds (cached browser and only the font packages the image lacks), and their bounds are re-recorded from a post-change run; the report slice's own growth (now about 12 minutes) is the remaining long pole.

tasks.title: A task's verdict is in its commit: Audit-Task, Audit-Gate, Audit-Run and Audit-Override trailers, written by the commit verb and read back from git alone
tasks.description:
The commit verb writes the verdict it bound the commit to into the commit itself. Today a task commit carries Audit-Row (a journal nonce) and an optional Co-Authored-By; which run graded it is known only through the evidence ledger and the journal. Add: Audit-Task: <task id>; Audit-Gate: <status> <gate digest>; Audit-Run: <runId>; and, when the verb was told to commit over a verdict, Audit-Override: <the reason, verbatim>. The values come from the one place that already decides them, the verdict binding the verb asks before it commits (_verdict_binding.binding): the trailers name the run the binding bound, never another, so a commit made in the phase tree after a wave member's bytes were integrated names the run that graded the phase tree's bytes. Audit-Row stays as it is.

Reading: _commit_trail.py gains the reader, over git log alone. A commit carrying Audit-Task and no Audit-Gate reads as no verdict recorded, never as passed. A commit carrying no Audit-Task (every commit made before this release, and every commit made by hand) is not a trailer commit and its verdict is read as before. Status (_status_facts.py) and the report (_evidence_view.py) read a done task's verdict at its commit from the trailers, and say which source they read.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. A task commit made by the verb in a real git fixture carries the trailers, and `git interpret-trailers --parse` returns them.
2. In a clone of that fixture with the evidence directory removed, the reader returns the same task, status, digest and run.
3. Audit-Task without Audit-Gate reads as no verdict recorded; a status word this build does not know is reported as itself, never folded into passed or failed.
4. An override reason is carried verbatim. Decide what a reason holding a newline does by what git round-trips (a folded trailer, or a refusal naming the line) and pin it with a case; a silent truncation is the defect.
5. Status and the report render the same verdict from the trailers as from the row, on one fixture read both ways.
6. A commit made over a tree other than the one the bound run graded is refused as today; the new trailers do not weaken that refusal.
7. COMPATIBILITY.md states the four trailer names as read from this release on, and that Audit-Row and the co-author trailer are unchanged; CHANGELOG.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md describe what the commit now carries.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: every reader of a task commit's message or trailers - _invariants.trailer_carriers and commits_carrying, the doctor's trail checks, drive-phase.py own_commit (it finds a task's commit through Audit-Row; it must keep working unchanged), close-phase.py, integrate-task.py, tools/check-git-pipeline.py (it drives the write half against a real repository and pins message shapes), and any suite asserting an exact commit message.

tasks.title: The newest run of a task or a phase is one record in its own shard, written by the gate under the phase lock
tasks.description:
Add the record that will replace the ledger row, beside the row, changing no reader yet. After a recorded run (run-test-gate.py --record, task or phase scope) the subject in its shard carries `lastRun`: the run's id, moments and durations (startedAt, durationMs, selectionMs), status and failed list, verdictSource and reusedFrom, the reuse key, the gate digest and source, leftToPhaseGate, the tested state (head, dirty, tree key), the banners and the machine and attribution lines, and per step: name, exit, ran, outcome, failing lines up to the existing cap, the measured duration when measured here, and reusedFrom when copied. A copied step carries its source's verdict fields forward, so the record is the newest measurement of each current step and no older record is needed to read it. `testEvidence` stays the three-key pointer and is written from the record in the same write. Replace, never append.

The write. Today the pointer write is skipped when the phase lock is held, because the ledger row stands anyway. A record that is the only copy cannot be skipped: the recorder takes the phase lock with a bounded wait behind any verb's write, and a record it still could not write is exit 3 naming the log path. Never exit 0 or 1 without the record. A verb that rewrites a task (move, reopen, group sign-off's copy of a carrier's pointer, reconcile) does to `lastRun` what it does to `testEvidence`.

The launch. `--launch <token>` is stored on the record, so a caller that started the run in the background can find the record of exactly that run.

Time. The recorder appends the gate and the selection stage to the task's `timing` itself, in the same locked write, from the same figures, citing the run by id; today the drive queues them in its own state from the ledger row. The stage survives the record's replacement.

ACCEPTANCE (each a case).
1. After five recorded runs of one gate a subject holds exactly one `lastRun`, its runId is the last one printed, and the shard is no larger than after the first run.
2. Exit 0 or 1 implies the shard's record names the printed runId and status; a lock that stays held past the wait is exit 3 naming the log, and the shard is unchanged.
3. `testEvidence` equals the pointer derived from `lastRun`; delete the pointer and reconcile restores it from the record.
4. A verb's write and a background record write, interleaved in both orders, both land: neither field is lost.
5. A recorded run changes no byte inside the content identity: the reuse key is the same before and after, and the set of paths the run modified (git status in a fixture) is exactly what recorded_paths names.
6. The record's size is bounded by the gate's width: failing lines per step at the existing cap, steps no more than declared plus derived. Print the measured bytes for this repository's own task gate in the outcome.
7. The schema accepts `lastRun` on a task and on a phase, a plan without it validates unchanged, and a one-file plan and a per-phase plan both carry it.
8. A machine path in a failing line reads scrubbed, as every string the shard write passes does, and the verdict fields are untouched.
9. The evidence row is still written, byte for byte as before, with the same runId as the record.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: every reader of a task or phase object that copies, renders or validates its keys - validate-manifest.py and _manifest_rules.py, _manifest_io's split and join, audit-task.py's verbs named above, render-report.py and the panel's composition (an unknown key must not be rendered as content), tools/demo/gen-demo-manifest.py and the committed examples, tools/check-committed-pii.py (the record holds a head and failing lines), tools/check-example-ledgers.py, and drive-phase.py's timing queue (queue_row, row_stages, stage_args): once the recorder writes the stages, the drive must not write them a second time.

Each step keeps name, exit, ran, outcome, failing lines cut at MAX_FAILING, durationMs only when measured here, and reusedFrom when copied. A REUSED row copies its source's steps forward; steps are cut at MAX_STEPS with stepsDropped. Also pointer_from_record and record_stages. write_record takes the phase lock with a bounded wait (RECORD_WAIT_SECONDS), reads the shard UNDER the lock, and writes lastRun, testEvidence and the task's gate+selection timing stages in one save_plan_json. It releases the lock only if it took it, then writes the testEvidence journal row. subject_records reads every record; reconcile restores a pointer from the record when the ledger holds no newer row. The redaction report (_mio.report_redactions) sits directly beside each save in write_pointer and write_record. Attempt 1 had moved it into the shared journal-row helper, which turned tests/test__manifest_io.py ex6 red; ex6 is now green. (b) run-test-gate --record builds the record (_run_record_of) and calls write_record. A record that is not written prints `record: NOT written - this run is only in <ledger file>` and exits 3 on a green AND a red run, at every exit site (verdict, all-left, empty gate, --json). New --launch TOKEN is stored on the record. (c) _task_timing: whole_ms, stamp_less, run_stages, append_run_stages (once per kind+runId). drive-phase: row_stages delegates to run_stages; queue_row queues only the wait stage for a gate run, because the recorder appends gate and selection; it still says whose stage a repeated verdict's is, read off the stages built. tasks.title: Every reader of recorded runs goes through one reader over the shard records and the older rows, and answers the same from either
tasks.description:
`_evidence_io.read_rows` is the seam every reader of recorded runs already goes through (count its callers with grep before you start and put the count's command in the outcome). Make what it returns the union of the frozen ledger rows and the `lastRun` records of the plan's subjects, each record presented in the row's shape, one entry per runId (a run present as both is one entry). Then prove that nothing downstream needs the ledger: for a fixture holding records only and the same fixture holding rows only, each of these gives the same answer - the verdict binding (_verdict_binding.binding, with its reused row followed to the measured source), the step repeat (reusable_run, repeated_step_sources, step_parts) and its part-reused result, the reading of a red against the base (base_run), latest_by_subject, row_by_run, the gate's mean, the drive's read-back of a run it launched (green and red, with no commit made, and a red read back runs no step), close-phase's reading of a branch's runs (it reads the branch's ledger texts through git today; it must read the branch's shards the same way), and audit-task's --failing-from and couple --basis-run (resolve against records and rows, or refuse naming both places).

The drive finds the record of the run it launched by the launch token, not by comparing the subject's run ids against a list kept in its own state.

With one record per subject, a rule written over 'the newest row for the identity' has only one candidate; where a branch can no longer be reached (a newer row for the same identity), delete it and its case rather than leaving it unreachable, and name each deleted branch in the outcome.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. The table: every reader named above, records-only against rows-only, same answer.
2. A second ask on an unchanged tree, with records only, measures exactly the steps the left-out reading names and copies every other, each copy naming a run that measured it.
3. A record whose reuse key is not the current key repeats nothing.
4. The drive's decision read from the record equals the run's own --json for green and for red, with no commit made; reading a red back runs no gate step.
5. A reader of history that finds no older directory says so with a basis; it never prints a zero as if it had counted.
6. A plan and ledger as the previous release wrote them (use a committed example or build the fixture from real rows) give the same status, report and gate-condition answers before and after this change.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: every caller of read_rows, row_by_run, latest_by_subject and oldest_first (the callers span the drive, the gate runner, audit-task.py, audit-lookup.py, full-gate.py, the doctor's trail and completion checks, the report, the panel, usage economics, propose-gates.py, validate-manifest.py's suite keys, record-outside-run.py, tools/plan-window.py, tools/gate-parity.py, tools/check-example-ledgers.py and the release guard under .claude/hooks). A caller that reads `rowFiles` or `files` to name where a run lives must still be able to: say what those mean for an entry that came from a shard.

tasks.title: The base is measured only when a red could predate the task, its verdict is kept per commit, and the writer is not held for it
tasks.description:
After a red task gate the drive measures the phase's base so that a red the base already has is not blamed on the task. Today that measurement is due whenever the reading is no-base or not-knowable, the red's decision is held until the base verdict exists, and the verdict lives in a base-scope ledger row, a progress record under the drive's state and a mark. State the rule as a property of the records and move the verdict where it survives.

Needed means all three: the task gate is red; some failing case or step is not one a file this task's `tests.add` created (a case the task itself added cannot predate it); and no clean-tree measurement of that step at that base commit is recorded. Otherwise no base run is started and the decision says which of the three made it unnecessary.

Kept means: the base verdict for a commit is in the plan (on the red task's record, keyed by the base commit, readable through the one reader), computed at most once per commit and step set, and a second red at the same base reads it.

Not held means: when a writer session exists to resume, the red's failing lines go to it at once, and the base runs beside it; if the base then shows the same red, the next decision says so and the writer is not resumed over it again. Where no session exists (the dispatched writer), the decision is offered with the base named as still running rather than withheld.

Keep what the phase before this one fixed: one liveness reading decides both the reading of a base run's record and the removal of its tree.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. A red whose failing cases all live in files the task's tests.add created starts no base run, and the decision says why.
2. A second red at the same base commit and step set starts no base run and reads the kept verdict, which equals the first.
3. A red with a session to resume sends the failing lines before the base verdict exists; a base that then shows the same red produces the base decision and no further resume over that red.
4. A base run killed mid-way leaves no tree and no claim behind after the next call, as today.
5. The seconds: print, for one red on this repository's own plan, the wall time from the red to the writer's resume before and after, measured twice with a gap.

tasks.title: A phase's CI run is in its shard at the sign-off commit, through one path from CI to the plan
tasks.description:
A phase's own gate verdict is on the phase already (its record and pointer). What graded the phase's commit on CI is not: the drive keeps the run it dispatched in its own state, and a red CI run reaches the plan as a bug through two call sites. Record on the phase `ci`: {runId, sha, conclusion, at}, written by one verb in the sign-off path, where sha is the head the run graded. A recorded red run files one bug naming the run and its failed jobs, through one module; reading the same run again files nothing. A run that cannot be read is refused and nothing is written. When CI has not reported by sign-off, the record says so (conclusion absent, with the basis) rather than being omitted.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. A signed-off fixture phase's shard carries ci with runId, sha and conclusion in the sign-off commit.
2. A recorded red run files one bug naming run and jobs; the same run read again files nothing.
3. An unreadable run is refused, exit non-zero, shard unchanged.
4. The bug-from-a-CI-run path is reached from one module only; name the call site removed.
5. The schema accepts the object and a plan without it validates unchanged.
6. Stated in the outcome as an orchestrator check, not a case: the recorded sha equals the head_sha GitHub reports for the recorded run.

tasks.title: A full-scope run's answer for a merged phase is in the plan, and a phase certified whole stays whole
tasks.description:
`meta.fullGate` names a third gate, and whether a merged phase has been certified whole by it is answered today by walking every full-scope ledger row for a green, measured, clean, verbatim run whose head contains the phase's merge. With one record per subject that walk has nothing to walk, and keeping only the last full run would turn a certified phase provisional the moment a later full run is red. Put the answer where it is asked: when a full run is recorded, each merged phase its head contains and that it certifies carries the certifying run (id, head, moment); a later red run removes no certification. `full_status` answers from those and from the frozen rows, with the same words (whole, provisional, stale, unknown) and the same bases. A plan that declares no fullGate reads and renders exactly as it does today.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. Over the existing table of full_status fixtures, the answer from the plan's own records equals the answer from the rows.
2. A phase certified by a green full run stays whole after a later red full run on a head that contains it.
3. A full run that could not be asked about (no mergedHead, ancestry not establishable) reads unknown with its basis, as today.
4. The release guard's reading of provisional phases is unchanged on its own cases.
5. A plan with no fullGate is byte-identical after a recorded task run.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: audit-status.py's provisional, stale-full-run and unknown-full-run conditions, _status_facts.py, render-report.py, the panel's state and areas, .claude/hooks/guard-release.py, the doctor's full-run check, full-gate.py's own recording and its learn path, and COMPATIBILITY.md's sentences about the full run.

tasks.title: No evidence row is written: the record in the shard is the only copy, and the older rows are frozen history
tasks.description:
Stop the writes. A recorded run of any scope appends no row, writes no anchor row to the journal for it and chains nothing; its record in the shard and, for a task, its commit's trailers are the record. The set of paths a recorded run writes (recorded_paths) loses the evidence directory, and every reader of that set follows through the one function: the reuse identity, the left-out reading and its names, the stamp's recorder exclusion, the scope digest, the commit scope and its label, and the landing refusal's evidence half. `evidence.dir` stays a read key: it is where the frozen rows are. Rows already written are never rewritten, migrated or deleted by this plugin, and a ledger written before this release keeps verifying.

Removed: import-evidence.py (the CI row adapter) and the gate runner's --writer; record-outside-run.py writes its subject's record instead of a row, or is removed if no caller remains (say which, with the grep).

COMPATIBILITY.md gains the major section's entries for this phase: the evidence file is no longer written; `testEvidence` stops meaning a cache of that file and is the pointer to the subject's record or to the run its commit names, and deleting the block is still always safe; --record's exit 3 means the shard record was not written; sign-off, done and close bind to the newest recorded run, a record or an older row; --failing-from and couple --basis-run resolve a record or an older row and no superseded run; tallies over history count one run per subject from this release on; the unknown-full-run arm about an unreadable ledger is restated. CHANGELOG.md says the first run after the upgrade measures every step, because the key no longer leaves the evidence directory out.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. A fixture phase driven from its first task to sign-off leaves the bytes under the evidence directory identical, and no task commit of it contains a path under that directory.
2. recorded_paths equals the set of paths a recorded run modifies, by git status in a fixture; the difference in the plan's meta across a recorded run is within the recorder's own keys.
3. On a plan and ledger as the previous release wrote them, status, the report, failing-tests and no-test-evidence answer the same after this change; with the ledger then deleted the two conditions still answer the same and the report says pointer without evidence, never failed.
4. The evidence boundary never moves later across the upgrade, and a record's moment never feeds it.
5. The doctor reports the trail from the plan and git, verifies a frozen ledger that is present, and says so when none is.
6. tools/check-example-ledgers.py, the demo generator and the committed examples are consistent with what the release writes: decide whether the examples keep a frozen ledger as history or carry records, state it, and keep `python3 tools/check-rendered-artifacts.py` green.
7. The code lines removed and added, by the plan's command, in the outcome.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: every caller of append_row, record and write_pointer; the journal's anchor row and whoever reads it (the doctor, audit-journal.py's merge and verify); _invariants.py's and commit-task-work.py's record paths; close-phase.py's ignored-stamp refusal; stamp-verification.py's recorder exclusion; tools/check-committed-pii.py, tools/check-rendered-artifacts.py and tools/check-git-pipeline.py (each names the evidence directory); SECURITY.md's fail-mode table if a row's write was in it; and the README or reference page that tells a user to commit the evidence directory.

tasks.title: Under the default configuration no per-call journal row and no preimage file is written, and a session's start clears what ended sessions left
tasks.description:
The hook that journals every Edit and Bash call writes a hash-chained row and, for a write, a preimage file. On this repository's own checkout the state directory they fill is measured in gigabytes and tens of thousands of files (print `du -sk .claude/state` and the file count in the outcome, before and after). Turn the per-call rows and the preimage files off by default: `journal.enabled` absent means off, true writes rows and verifies exactly as before, and the key keeps being read. The rows the plugin's own verbs write when they change the plan (a task moved, a bug filed, the commit's Audit-Row) are not per-call rows and are unchanged by this task: a task's commit must still be found by the drive under the default configuration, and a case holds that. The session-start sweep removes preimage files and the state files of sessions that have ended and keeps the live session's.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. Under the default configuration an Edit and a Bash call write no journal row and no preimage file.
2. With journal.enabled true the rows are written and verify as before.
3. tools/bench-hooks.py --gate is green, and the disabled path imports only what the hook floor already imports.
4. After the sweep, a fixture state directory holding files of ended sessions and of the live one holds only the live one's; nothing outside the plugin's own state names is removed.
5. A verb's own journal row and a task commit's Audit-Row are written under the default configuration, and the drive finds that commit.
6. COMPATIBILITY.md records the changed default in the major section without removing the key; SECURITY.md's fail-mode table and the config reference say what the default now is and what turning it on restores.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: every reader of journal.enabled (hooks/_config.py's defaults, the doctor's trail checks, the panel's settings and help text, the config schema and the example config), restore points if they read preimages (say whether they do, with the grep), verify-invariants.py's checks that read per-call rows, the usage meter's session files, and any document that tells a user the journal records every tool call.

tests/test_meter_usage.py: the session-start sweep removes preimage files and state files of ended sessions, keeps the live session's and touches nothing outside the plugin's own state names
tests/test__journal_io.py: a verb's own row is written under the default configuration

outcome.technical: THE THREE VALUES. journal.enabled is read three ways: DEFAULTS carries None (a bool default would be erased by the deep merge); _config._journal_switch returns True/False/None (non-bool -> None); journal_records_calls(cfg) is True only for true and gates every per-call path in journal-writes.py (manifest.edit, config.edit, derived task.complete/task.commit/phase.signoff, bash.unsandboxed, pre-image slots); journal_enabled(cfg) stays on unless false and gates the verbs' and the panel's own rows, so a task commit's Audit-Row row and the drive's commit lookup work under the default (vr1, vr2). The last will: an edit or Bash write of the config is still judged against its pre-image while recording is off, so true->false and true->unset (key deleted) are journalled; the summary now names the key as each document holds it ('journal.enabled true->unset', k1b). atomic_write_text no longer imports tempfile, so the disabled path imports only the floor (do4, k10b). FIXTURES SPLIT. tests/test_audit_task.py hw29 is about the hook's own rows: per-call recording on purpose, no twin. tests/test_guard_bash_writes.py got recording for free before: kcfg and cfg_sr are now the default, kcfg_rec/cfg_sr_rec (true) are used only for k1/k2's and sr3's real journal-writes append; default twin k4 (the same edit under the default makes no append and leaves no claim). tools/check-git-pipeline.py: g8-g10 exercise the per-call recorder, the fixture config is written after the seed commit (g15 stays clean); default twin g8z drives journal-writes through py-launch.sh with the config set aside: both passes exit 0, no row, no pre-image. tests/test_journal_writes.py fixtures that drive main() write journal.enabled true (_RECORDING/_recording_config); default cases do1-do4. PANEL. settings.js boolField: def = dv===undefined || dv===true, so the payload's null draws journal.enabled unticked (HEAD's code drew it ticked and unticking wrote false); ticking back to what the file held restores the held value, so an explicit false is not silently turned into unset. Node probe of the extracted functions: unset shows unticked, toggle -> true, back -> {}; true shows ticked, toggle -> {}, back -> true; false shows unticked, toggle -> true, back -> false. _panel_settings.py help text names unset/true/false and that the commands' and panel's rows are still written; label 'Also record each tool call's plan and config writes'; blurb updated. Cases js1 (build_state payload: defaults.journal.enabled null, config key absent), js2 (help and label), js3 (source pin on boolField's expression, labelled as a source property). count-ui-pins showed no existing pin on boolField or this field; test__panel_page/test__panel_ui/test_panel_server/test__panel_write green, vitest 858/858. Only a browser confirms the box is painted unticked and a click writes the draft; not run by me. The orchestrator re-captured screenshots in this checkout: only docs/screenshots/captured-at.json changed (panel digest adaffbe8...), no PNG bytes changed. SWEEP RULES. meter-usage SessionEnd writes session-ended-<id>.json; SessionStart (_config.sweep_session_state) removes only .json files directly in stateDir named by _config.SESSION_STATE_PREFIXES plus a session key with a '.'/'-' boundary: every file of a session a marker names; and, while calls are not recorded, every pre-image except the live session's and a not-ended session's config slot (CONFIG_PREIMAGE_DIGEST, pinned to sha256(CONFIG_REL)[:12] by jrc3). A session without a marker is never known to be live: it is treated as possibly running and keeps its files until detect-plan-skip's 7-day age-out, which now reads the same tuple (_GC_PREFIXES = _config.SESSION_STATE_PREFIXES; g8 derives every '<prefix>%s...json' literal under hooks/ and scripts/ and requires each in the tuple). A resumed session clears its own marker and keeps its state (sw4); resumed after another session's start it finds its state gone and starts fresh, its own start removing only a peer's non-config pre-images (sw6). A peer whose edit began with recording on and turned it off keeps its config slot through another session's start, and its Post still writes the last will (sw5, driven through the real journal-writes hook). Other pre-images are read only while recording is on; a double flip inside one call leaves the Post with no pre-image, which seeds and claims nothing, and verify reports drift. Cursors live under ledgerDir and are untouched (sw2). DOCTOR. _doctor_trail._per_call_row adds an OK line under 'journal calls': on (true), off with basis unset-the-default, off with basis false, or a non-bool named and read as unset; never a finding (dt13b, dt13c); the was-running warning's fix now separates removing false from setting true. TEXT SURFACES. COMPATIBILITY.md section 2 Promised paragraph 'journal.enabled breaks this promise in 4.0.0, a major' (the key is kept and still read); CHANGELOG Unreleased Breaking entry; SECURITY.md audit-trail lead, bash.unsandboxed sentence and the journal-writes/meter-usage fail-mode rows; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE journal-writes, meter-usage and guard-secrets-read sections; reference/config.md section with the three-value table; schema descriptions; example config (enabled omitted so a copy gets the default, comment says how to write true or false); README hook bullet, stale-state bullet, trail bullet, guarantee row, config row (default unset), Audit trail opening and the three-value paragraph; _help.py summary and paragraph (t11b). The five further surfaces: guard-secrets-read.py docstring sentence and one user-facing message string only ('With journal.enabled true the unsandboxed run is journalled either way.'), no logic touched; reference/execute-task.md completion-rows bullet; reference/manifest-conventions.md lines on the hook's rows and pre-images; reference/verbs-in-full.md two derived-row sentences; docs/handbook.html trail paragraph (hand-written: nothing in tools/ or the repo writes it). docs/research/pipeline-cost-design.md left as a dated record. MEASUREMENTS. This checkout's .claude/state: du -sk .claude/state -> 3012872 KB; find .claude/state -maxdepth 1 -type f | wc -l -> 44287 files, of which find ... -name 'journal-preimage-*' | wc -l -> 42787, summing (find ... -print0 | xargs -0 du -k) to 2982384 KB. Earlier the same session: 2987712 KB / 44961 files, then 3012864 KB / 45311 files about an hour later. A read-only dry run of the sweep logic said it would remove 30520 files (2055274 KB). This repo's config has no journal block, so per-call recording is off here under the new default. MUTATIONS (throwaway copy, __pycache__ purged): old default reader -> do1, do3, do3b, do4, jrc1, jrc2, vr1, k4, g8z, dt13b, dt13c red; live not protected -> sw1, sw4; pre-images kept when off -> sw1; removed when on -> sw3; boundary dropped -> sw1, sw3; no end marker -> sw1, sw3; config-slot spare removed -> sw1, sw5; wrong digest -> jrc3, sw5; old GC list or a prefix dropped from the tuple -> g8; tempfile back -> k10b, do4. GATES. Full python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py exit 0: 197/197 files ok, 19290 cases. Task gate (five files) exit 0, 1154 cases. check-git-pipeline 0, bench-hooks --gate 0 (3.14.7 only; 3.8-3.13 not measured, no interpreter here), check-rendered-artifacts --before-commit 0, gate-parity 0, check-example-ledgers 0, ruff clean, vermin -t=3.8- clean. The defect found on the way (a bool field whose default is missing from the defaults payload is drawn ticked, ci.pushCarry) is recorded by the orchestrator outside this task and not fixed here.
outcome.descriptive: An unset journal.enabled now records no tool call and keeps no pre-image (the verbs' and panel's rows still written), a session start clears what ended sessions left, and every surface states the new default.

tasks.title: A case that compares two gate runs' printed lines says which line differed, and its Windows-only red has a named cause
tasks.description:
One case of tests/test_run_test_gate.py, pgo7, failed once on a Windows CI runner (run 44363694425, job "selftests (windows, plain 2)") over product code that passed it on the same runner image in two other runs the same day. The case runs a task's gate once with executor.phaseGateOnly absent and once with it empty and asserts that the two print the same lines once ids and times are masked. In the failing run both exited 0 with the same steps and the same row keys, so the difference is in the printed lines, and the failure message does not show them. A case that reddens a green tree once in three runs is how a CI verdict stops being read.

Do this in order. First, make the case's failure say what differed: when the masked line lists are unequal, the message carries the first differing pair of lines (and the lengths if they differ), so the next red of this case names its own cause. Second, read the failing job's log (gh run view --job with the job's id from that run, read-only) for anything the run printed around the case, and read the case's mask against every line the gate prints: a duration that changes unit between two runs (ms to s), a count of workers or slots, a path under a temp directory with a random part, a line that appears only when a step crosses a time threshold, the order of two lines written by different streams. Third, fix the cause where it is: if a line legitimately varies with time, the mask must cover its whole varying part; if a line appears or not depending on timing, the two runs are not comparable on that line and the case must say so rather than compare it; if the product prints something nondeterministic that a user would also see vary, that is a product fix and belongs in run-test-gate.py.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. With the two line lists made to differ in one line (a mutation in a scratch copy, restored in the same command), the failure message names that line pair.
2. The cause is named in the outcome with the evidence that it is the cause (the log line, or the unmasked form found by reading), or stated as not established with what was ruled out; a mask widened without a named cause is not accepted.
3. The case still fails when executor.phaseGateOnly set to an empty list changes what a task's run prints: prove it by mutation.
4. The suite is green under the sweep and under the cp1252 leg locally (python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_run_test_gate.py, and the same with --encoding cp1252).

DEPENDANTS: the suite's other cases that share pgo7's masking helper, if it is shared.

outcome.technical: tests/test_run_test_gate.py only; run-test-gate.py is unchanged. (1) New _first_line_difference(left, right, width=160): returns None when the two texts have the same lines, otherwise 'line K differs: <left> / <right>' with each side cut to width, plus both line counts when they differ. pgo7's label now ends with 'printed lines, absent / empty: <that, or the same>'. (2) CAUSE, reproduced: the step line is '  %-12s exit %-3d %10s  %s' (run-test-gate.py:5047), so the duration is right-aligned in a 10-wide column. _pgo_masked collapsed each digit run to N but kept the padding, which still encodes the digit count. A step at 111 ms in one fixture and 73 ms in the other masks to '      N ms' against '       N ms'. Raw diff seen locally under load: 'sweep exit 0       111 ms' / 'sweep exit 0        73 ms'. Unloaded, steps here take about 30 ms and never cross 100 ms, so the case passes; on CI, trivial steps sit near 100 ms (pr3 in the failing Windows run 44363694425 printed row=156 for a row of one trivial measured step). pgo7 was red in 44363694425 (windows plain 2), 44366022835 and 44388480667 (linux stress 1). Runs 44385960921 and 44397426313, named in the hand-off, carry only vt8, not pgo7. The CI log prints no text for pgo7, so the CI instance itself is not observed line by line; the mechanism is reproduced, and the next red will name its own line pair. (3) FIX in the mask, not the product: the duration field (the spaces before it, the number and the unit, in every form _fmt.human_duration renders, _fmt.py:187-193: N ms, N.N s, N m NN s) becomes one ' <duration>' token, applied before the digit collapse. The column is intended product behaviour (run-test-gate.py:5039-5045 states why it is right-aligned), so no product change is owed. A check over 13 durations from 0 ms to one hour gave a single masked line. Ruled out by reading: the 'machine:' line reads only the fixture project's own rows and journal (run-test-gate.py:5548-5579, _evidence_io.py merge_seams/shared_the_machine), and each fixture is its own git project, so no concurrent sibling reaches it; the reach-reading clocks are 30 s and 120 s (_affected_tests.py:1305-1306); the root path is not printed on this path. ACCEPTANCE 1: a scratch copy of the suite rewrites one line of the empty-setting text, and pgo7 fails with: line 11 differs: 'GATE GREEN: sweep, browser, tree unchanged' / 'GATE GREEN: sweep, browser, tree CHANGED'. The first attempt at (a) and (b) keyed on the parsed names and SURVIVED, because phase_gate_only_setting returns ((), None) for absent and for empty alike (_config_rules.py:319-328), so it fired in both arms. Re-keyed on the config key, both went red. ACCEPTANCE 4: every gate command listed exits 0 (701 cases each for the suite; 1497 cases across the orchestrator's 5-file list); ruff and vermin also pass on the file. tasks.title: A branch's first CI run restores the browser install: the default branch seeds the cache, the install is written once, a partial set fetches what it names and a bad entry heals
tasks.description:
The browser jobs now restore the Chromium download and the system packages the runner image lacks from a cache, and the first measurement shows what that buys and what it does not. A cache entry is saved only by a job that succeeded, and an entry is readable by the branch that saved it and by branches cut from the default branch's entries. The default branch's push runs skip the browser jobs when the commit is already verified, so the default branch saves no entry, and every phase's CI branch misses both caches on its first run. On a miss the archive is asked for about as many megabytes as before the change (the package index plus the font packages), so on a day the runner's mirror is slow the first run of a branch still pays minutes; the two runs measured so far had a fast mirror and differ by seconds. The review of that change also found three things in its shell.

Make a hit the ordinary case, and make the steps do what their names say:
1. Seed. The default branch holds a saved entry for both keys after any push that changes a key's inputs (the playwright pin in the lock file, the runner image version, the list of packages the image lacks), so a branch's first run restores it. Do it with the least new machinery that is honest: a job that runs only the install steps and saves the caches, on the default branch, when no entry for the key exists. It carries a time bound and a `longest` line like every job, and tools/gate-parity.py's rules must hold it (a job outside the slices: say how the parity rules read it, and extend them if they cannot).
2. One install, written once. The two browser jobs and the seeding job run the same steps; today the block is written out twice with a comment asking that both be changed together. Put it in one place the three jobs call (a composite action under .github/actions/ is the established form), or hold the copies to one text with a gate-parity rule that names a difference. A prose rule is not enough.
3. A partial set fetches what it names. When some but not all packages are in the restored set, the step downloads the missing ones and their dependencies and nothing else, and the check that decides a package is present covers the dependencies the install needs, not only the packages named. The step's title and log line say what the code does.
4. A bad entry heals. The system-packages key carries the runner's architecture as the browser key does. When installing from a restored set fails, the step falls back once to fetching from the archive and says so; a job is red only when that also fails. A manual version token in the key lets an operator retire an entry.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. The orchestrator dispatches runs for you as before (hand back READY-FOR-RUN with what to read, do not file): a run on the default-branch path that saves the entries, and a first run of a fresh branch that restores both. State what each line of each log must show.

One case of tests/test__commit_trail.py, vt8, is red on Windows CI and green everywhere else: it failed in "selftests (windows, plain 2)" in both runs that carried the verdict-trailers commit (44379408461 and 44380971983), with "FAIL vt8 a FOLDED trailer reads as git unfolds it - the line break and its indent become one space - which is why the writer refuses a reason holding a line break rather than folding it: 'first half' / ['first half']". So on that runner the reader returned only the first line of a folded trailer value, where the case expects git's unfolded value. The reader asks git for `%(trailers:only,unfold)`; what differs on Windows is not established: the git version on the runner image, a carriage return in the commit message the fixture writes (a `\r\n` line end makes the continuation line something other than a folded line), or how the fixture hands the message to git there.

This matters beyond the case: the product's reader of a commit's verdict must read the same value on every platform a plan is driven on, and a reason that the WRITER refuses to fold can still arrive folded from a commit written by hand or by another tool.

Do this in order. First establish the cause with evidence, without a Windows machine: read the failing job's log for the git version (read-only gh calls on those two runs), read how the fixture writes the message (text mode, newline translation, `-F` file against `-m`), and reproduce the Windows shape here by writing the same bytes Windows would write (a `\r\n` message through `git commit -F`, and `core.autocrlf` as the runner sets it) and reading it back with the reader. Third, a case that is red here, on this platform, for the cause you found (the reproduction above), so the next regression does not need a Windows runner to be seen.
