tasks.title: The browser install's shell is guarded in the repository, its seed path is seen on a real runner, and a seed cannot redden a verified push
tasks.description:
The browser install now lives in one composite action (.github/actions/browser-install/action.yml) that both browser jobs call, and on a push to the default branch whose commit is already verified those jobs run it with `seed` true and skip their slice. The review of that change left three things that must not ship as they are, and two smaller ones that belong with them.

1. Nothing in the repository guards the action's shell. It was developed against a stub harness (fake sudo with an ownership ledger, fake apt, dpkg, cache directories; twenty cases, seven mutations) that was never committed, so the only check of the shell is a real CI run, and a bug on the hit path falls into the fallback and leaves the job green with one warning: the regression the change removed can come back with every gate green. Commit the harness as a check this repository runs: its cases execute the action's own `run:` blocks, read out of the committed action.yml (never a copy of the shell), against the stubs. Choose its home by this repository's rules rather than by habit: a `tests/test_<name>.py` must name a module that exists (the coverage classifier reports an orphan), tools under tools/ carry their own cases and are swept, and the gate set is what `sh tools/verify.sh --list` prints, held to the workflow by tools/gate-parity.py. It must include the case that fails when a full hit falls back (a hit that fetches is red, not a warning), the ownership case that reproduces the runner's "Permission denied" on the first version of the action, and one case per seed decision. It must run on macOS and Linux and under the sweep's isolation (scratch cwd, HOME and TMPDIR; no network; no real sudo, apt or dpkg). State in its docstring what class of runner behaviour the stubs cannot see.

2. The seed path ran on no real runner: every probe was a dispatch, where `seed` is false and the lookup steps are skipped. Before filing, hand back READY-FOR-RUN with a probe-only patch (a separate diff from the task's own, clearly marked, that hard-wires `seed` true for the two browser jobs on a dispatch) and the lines to read; the orchestrator commits the task's diff plus that patch to a probe branch and dispatches twice: the first run must look both keys up, find none, install and save; the second must find both, install nothing and save nothing. The probe-only patch is never part of the task's diff.

3. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md says a verified push to the default branch runs only tools/ci-verified.py. That was exact before the change and is false now: say what runs (two browser jobs that look the cache up and, on a miss, install and save) and what it costs.

4. A seed must not turn a verified push red for a cache it did not need, and must not fail silently either. Today npm ci, the dry run and (on a miss) apt run before and after the seed decision, and any of them failing fails the job on the default branch. Decide and state the rule: on the seed path a failure is an annotation a reader of the run sees, the job's conclusion does not redden the run, and the slice path is untouched (a failure there is red as before). If that needs `continue-on-error`, tools/gate-parity.py does not read a step's `continue-on-error` today: extend the reader so a step that carries the slice can never be the one that is allowed to fail, with a red case and an allow case.

5. The parity reader's new step-condition cases write the `- if:`-first form; the workflow uses `- name:` first with a following `if:`. Add the pin for the form the workflow uses.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. The committed check is red on the action as it stood at the first probe (the ownership defect) and on a hit that falls back, each proven by mutation of a scratch copy of the action, restored in the same command; green on the action as it is.
2. The two probe runs show the seed path's two branches on a real runner, and the outcome quotes the lines.
3. `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` and the sweep over the tools this task touches are green; `sh tools/verify.sh --list` shows the new check in a slice a per-run CI job runs, and the job's bound still has its `longest` basis.
4. On a dispatch and on a pull request the browser slices run exactly as before (the reviewer checked this for the current tree; say what in your diff could change it and why it does not).
5. The guide's sentence is exact.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: tools/gate-parity.py's slice, bound and step-condition rules; tools/verify.sh's slices and CONTRIBUTING.md/CLAUDE.md where they list gates (CLAUDE.md is outside the files: say what sentence there, if any, is no longer exact); the sweep's isolation rules for a tool under tools/; tools/lints/_deps.py's layer and enumeration lints if the new file needs a row (hand back the exact row BEFORE filing if a file you need is outside your list).

tasks.title: A shard has one lock every writer takes and reads behind: the run record, the pointer and reconcile go through one helper, and a repeated verdict's record says where its steps came from
tasks.description:
The run record (`lastRun` in a task's or phase's shard, with `testEvidence` derived from it) is written by the gate under the phase lock. Its review showed that this is not the lock that serialises writers of a shard: every audit-task.py verb writes the shard under the `index` lock, and the phase lock is held only by `start`'s claim and the drive's phase run. A probe held the index lock as a verb does; the record was written after 0.02 s without waiting, and the verb's later write from its earlier read left neither `lastRun` nor `testEvidence`; in the other order the verb's write is lost. The case meant to hold this (lr4) passes because its stand-in verb takes the phase lock, which no real verb does, and lr5 asserts what the test's own read-modify-write does. CHANGELOG.md, manifest-conventions.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md state "neither write loses the other's key", which is false today. Everything later in this phase reads the record, so this is fixed before any reader moves.

THE INVARIANT, to hold by mechanism and not by a list of call sites: a shard has one lock that every writer of it takes, and every writer reads the shard AFTER taking it. Find which lock that is by reading what the verbs do (`_under_lock`, `acquire_index_lock`), not by what the record's first design said, and make the record's write, the pointer's write (`write_pointer` still reads the shard before it takes its lock) and reconcile obey it through ONE helper that takes the lock, reads, lets the caller change the node, and saves; no function in _evidence_io.py saves a shard outside that helper. Whether the phase lock is still taken as well is yours to decide and to state with its reason and with the one fixed order in which two locks are taken (a second order anywhere is a deadlock); say what a gate launched by the drive, which runs while the drive's own phase run holds the phase lock, does under your rule. The bounded wait stays: a live holder is waited for up to the bound, and a record that still cannot be written exits 3 as now.

Then the rest of the review:
1. A repeated verdict's record. When the gate repeats an earlier run's verdict instead of measuring, the record's steps are copied from the ledger row of the source run; with no such row the record is `steps: []` under `verdictSource: reused` with nothing saying the steps are missing, and no case covers the arm at all (replacing the copy with an empty list left both suites green, because every record case runs with --no-reuse). A later task of this phase stops writing ledger rows, so the ledger cannot be the source. The run being repeated is, by the reuse rule, the subject's newest run, which is the record this write replaces: take the steps from the record being replaced when it is that run, from the ledger row otherwise, and when neither holds them say so in the record in a field a reader cannot mistake for an empty run. Settle with the schema what `startedAt` and `durationMs` mean on a repeated run (the schema says `startedAt` is absent there; the code keeps the read-back's own) and make code, schema and documents say one thing. Cases: the repeated arm with the source in the replaced record, with the source only in the ledger, and with neither.
2. Two writers of one key. When a ledger row is stamped after the record (a record write that was refused), reconcile moves only the pointer, so `testEvidence` and `lastRun` name different runs, against "the two always name one run" in manifest-conventions.md and COMPATIBILITY.md's sentence about the values `testEvidence` caches. Decide which is true: reconcile rewrites the record from the row it trusts, or the documents say when the two may differ and what a reader does then. One of them changes.
3. Text: the `--record` help and the comment beside the unrecorded exit say a green run; a red run exits 3 as well. The refusal printed for a dead lock holder reads "...use audit-lock --takeover, then nothing was written to the plan" and names no repair in an order a reader can follow: say what happened, then what to run.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. A case drives a REAL verb of audit-task.py (not a stand-in that takes a lock by name) against a record write, in both orders, with the verb held inside its locked section by the test: both writes land, and the record's write waited. It is red at HEAD.
2. A case fails if any function in _evidence_io.py saves a shard outside the one helper (read the module's AST or prove it by mutation; say which).
3. The three repeated-verdict cases above; the mutation that empties the copied steps is red.
4. Mutations, each in a scratch copy outside every checkout, restored in the same command, __pycache__ purged, the mutation confirmed landed: the lock replaced by the phase lock alone; the read moved before the lock in each of the three writers; the wait set to 0; the lock order swapped if two are taken.
5. The documents say what the code does: search every place that states the lock or "neither write loses" (CHANGELOG.md, manifest-conventions.md, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, COMPATIBILITY.md, the schema's descriptions, help text) and list in the outcome each place changed.
6. Timing: the gate's own run must not get slower by a wait it does not need. Measure `run-test-gate.py --record` on a small fixture plan before and after, twice each with a gap, and report the four figures.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: the drive's read-back of a background gate and its timing queue; `audit-task.py` verbs that write a task node while a gate of that task runs (`note`, `scope`, `done`, group sign-off's copy of the record); reconcile and the doctor's evidence checks; the panel's writes through `_panel_write` (same lock?); the sweep's isolation (a suite that takes the index lock in a scratch project); Windows, where a lock file's rename and a held handle behave differently (say what your change does there and which existing case covers it).

If a file you need is outside your list, stop BEFORE filing and hand back the exact change.

outcome.technical: ONE LOCK, ONE HELPER: every plan-file write in _evidence_io (pointer, record, reconcile, evidence boundary) goes through write_plan_file(project, path, change, note, session_id, wait, outcome, repair, config) under SHARD_LOCK='index' - the lock every audit-task verb (_under_lock), the panel (_panel_write.LOCK_NAME) and close-phase take - reading the file only after the acquire; lk1/lk2/lk3 hold it by AST. The phase lock is NOT taken: it claims a phase's run and guards no write, and one lock leaves no order to keep. It is one lock per PLAN, not per shard: every plan-file write excludes every other; measured on a copy of this repo's plan (373 KB index, 336 KB P169 shard), two rounds 50 s apart: solo hold 99-121 ms; a wave of three started together 122-431 ms per member, of six at most 845/824 ms; every record landed, so a wave of three cannot reach RECORD_WAIT_SECONDS (30 s) on this machine; a member waiting past it exits 3 with its ledger row written. Lock behaviour: a record waits RECORD_WAIT_SECONDS for a live holder, then exits 3 green or red; pointer/reconcile/boundary wait WAIT_SECONDS; a verb behind a record waits its own WAIT_SECONDS (unchanged); a dead holder is never taken over and the refusal says what happened, then audit-lock.py release index --force, then the re-run; a held phase lock refuses nothing any more. REPEATS: repeat_carried/record_carrying carry repeatedRun and the steps from the ledger row, else from the replaced record under the lock, else repeatedRunUnread {runId, basis}; a reader asks repeatedRun first; a whole repeat has no startedAt and its own durationMs/selectionMs (schema, guide, conventions say the same). reconcile rewrites lastRun from a newer ledger row in the pointer's write. Text: --record help and E_UNRECORDED comment say green or red; the unrecorded line names the index lock. Group sign-off (audit-task.py _group_record) now carries the repeated run when the ledger or plan holds it (grc1-grc3). DRIVE BOUND (finding P169-R30): cancelled_gate in drive-phase.py is the one decision for the task gate and the phase gate; the count is the launch mark's cancelledBefore, carried when a relaunch replaces the mark, gone when a verdict spends it; CANCELLED_BOUND = 2 (UNMEASURED_BOUND's count, for its reason); below it the gate is relaunched under a new token with no attempt spent, at it the drive asks gate-cancelled (rerun|block) or phase-gate-cancelled (rerun|decline), and the ask stays open; rerun drops the mark (count from zero), block blocks with the reason. bg4 now pins dispatch-again under a new token (its wait arm deleted: the killed run's record now lands, so wait cannot be reached), cb1-cb7 the bound. Dependants: wait-gate read-back reads the cancelled record; each cancelled run's stages are appended once by its own record write (record_stages excludes only repeats), which is right since each ran; a resumed session whose gate was SIGTERMed counts one on the first next, a SIGKILLed gate leaves no record and stays wait-gate as before; a wave member's mark and parked ask are its own, so the bound is per member (not tested in a wave fixture); --explain prints the decide text with no run: line (cb1); a loop on next --signal sees `audit P1 ask P1.1 | gate-cancelled: ... | next: next P1 --signal --answer rerun|block ...` with no run: line, the same on every call, so it ends only if it stops on a non-dispatch verb; auto ends at the ask instead of relaunching (the relaunch's new token had defeated AUTO_REPEAT_BOUND). orchestrator.md names one sibling ask in a pointer sentence to execute-task.md (which now carries gate-cancelled); it is not an enumeration and has 13 bytes left under measure-context's ceiling, so no row was added; measure-context --gate unchanged from HEAD (GATE OK, every figure identical). Docs: CHANGELOG, COMPATIBILITY, guide, manifest-conventions, schema, README (an invariant row and the refused-record paragraph), doctor.md, panel.md, execute-task.md, verbs-in-full.md, handbook.html, _panel_runstate.py comment; gen-demo-manifest exemption row. One rewrite of write_evidence_since in _evidence_io.py was made through a Bash python script rather than the Edit tool. Mutations (scratch export, landing confirmed, pycache purged, restored, cmp clean): 18 rows all killed - lock is phase lock alone; read before lock in helper/record/pointer/reconcile; wait=0; copied steps emptied; reconcile writes no record; save outside helper; group copy without source; record_carrying ignores ledger; help says green only; cancel count never carried (task, phase); bound never reached; bound reached at once (allow); count survives a verdict; rerun keeps the mark. Runs: task gate 3/3 files ok 2366 cases; test_drive_phase alone 1039 ok; extra suites 6/6 ok 1005; test__panel_runstate 44 ok; check-rendered-artifacts --before-commit 0, check-example-ledgers 0, check-git-pipeline 0; measure-context --gate OK; full sweep 198/198 files ok, 19367 cases. Gate timing --record before/after: 472/263 ms vs 215/222 ms (round one before was a cold start).
outcome.descriptive: A gate's record and a verb's write of one plan file no longer lose each other, a repeated verdict's record says where its steps came from, and a gate that keeps being killed stops the drive with an ask instead of looping.

tasks.title: The record is sufficient for every reader of the one seam: the drive finds its run after a replacement, readers read the plan they were handed, the importer takes a run held only as a record, and an unreadable shard is said as that
tasks.description:
Readers of a test-gate run now go through one seam (`_evidence_io.read_rows`) that finds a run in the plan's record as well as in the ledger. An independent review of that change found no case where a record-only run makes the commit binding accept what the ledger would have refused, and four things that are wrong or will be the moment ledger rows stop being written, which a later task of this phase does. They are fixed here, before that task.

1. The drive loses the run it launched. The launch token is only on the record; the ledger row never carries it and the union adds it to a row only while the record still holds that same run. When another run of the same subject is recorded after the launched one, or the launched run's record write was refused, the drive answers wait-gate with "no gate row ... since" for good, though the ledger holds the row. Put the token on the ledger row too, and for the time when no row is written: when the subject's newest run is later than the launch and carries another token, the drive says the launched run was replaced, by which run, and what to do, instead of waiting. Cases for both orders (the existing case covers only the foreign run landing first).

2. The record is not yet sufficient for the seam's readers. A run held only as a record gives `followersOwed`, `gateReach` and its not-asked twin, `observations`, `treeMutated` and `coverage` as None or empty with nothing saying so: the drive decides a red that owes regenerated followers as a plain red, a repeated verdict prints that its source recorded no reach reading, the panel and the report say no comparison was made. The record's keys are a hand list beside the readers. Make sufficiency a mechanism: the record carries what the seam's readers read, and a case fails when a reader of the seam takes a row key the record does not carry (derive the readers' keys by reading the code that consumes the seam, or hold an explicit table that a case compares with a real row written by the gate; say which and why). Mind the record's size bound: say what each added field costs on this repository's own task gate, and what is cut first when a run is over the bound.

3. Callers read the wrong plan. `run-test-gate.py` (several call sites), `audit-task.py`'s `_ledger_run` and `_runs_under`, and the importer's `held_runs` call the seam with no plan path, so the records read are those of the plan the project's config names while the record is written to the plan the command was handed; in a project holding more than one plan (this repository's examples), reuse and a repeat's source are looked up in a foreign plan whose task ids collide. Make the plan a REQUIRED argument of the seam, so a caller that forgets it is an error, and hand every caller the plan it was handed. A case with two plans in one project whose task ids collide: a run recorded for one is not reused for, bound to, or found from the other.

4. The importer refuses too much. It refuses a whole ledger file when any of its runs is held as a record, which is the ordinary state of a project whose plan travels with git and whose evidence files do not: the run recorded on another machine arrives in the committed shard first, and that machine's ledger file can then never be imported. Only a run held as a ledger ROW is a duplicate; a run held only as a record is imported and the union's rule decides which copy a reader sees. Rewrite the two cases the earlier change added (they pin the refusal) and say in COMPATIBILITY.md or the CHANGELOG, whichever states the importer's behaviour, what it does.

5. Messages and unreadable shards. `--base-of`, the drive's `ledger_row`, the binding and the panel's dangling sentence (plugins/audit/scripts/ui/panel/overview.js) name the ledger alone or print a zero nobody counted; a shard that will not read is skipped silently by close-phase's `tip_bodies` and `branch_records` and ignored by the importer, and three functions walk a plan's shards with three error rules (`plan_bodies`, `subject_records`, `tip_bodies`). One walker, one rule for a shard that will not read (it is reported with its file, and a reader that cannot tell "no run" from "could not read" says could not read), and each message names both places it looked. For the panel's sentence read the `refactoring-the-assembled-ui` skill and run `python3 tools/count-ui-pins.py` BEFORE editing; the change there is the sentence and what it reads, nothing else; you cannot run the browser gates, so say which pins and which non-browser suites cover it.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. Each of points 1 to 4 has a case red at HEAD and green after; the mutations that prove them are run in a scratch copy outside every checkout, restored in the same command, __pycache__ purged, each confirmed landed.
2. With a fixture plan whose ledger directory is REMOVED after the runs are recorded, every reader of the seam answers as it does with the ledger present, or says what it could not read: the commit binding (accept and refuse), the gate's reuse, the drive's read-back and its followers, `--failing-from`, `couple --basis-run`, close-phase, status, the report's and the panel's evidence facts. One case per reader, or one table-driven case that names each.
3. The previous release's plan (no record anywhere; examples/acme-store as committed) gives byte-identical status, `--gate` and report output before and after, as the earlier change showed for itself.
4. `python3 tools/check-rendered-artifacts.py --before-commit` and `python3 tools/check-example-ledgers.py` exit 0; a committed page your change makes stale is handed back BEFORE filing.
5. The record's bytes on this repository's own widest task gate, before and after, measured twice.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: the commit verb and `_verdict_binding`; the gate's reuse and `--base-of`; the drive (read-back, followers, timing queue, wave members' trees: which plan does a member's gate read and write?); close-phase and integrate; `audit-task.py` `--failing-from`, `couple`, group sign-off; the importer and docs/examples' CI pipelines that call it; status, the report and the panel's evidence view; the doctor's evidence and trail checks; the demo generator's schema exemptions and the schema's `lastRun` description (a field added to the record is described there); reconcile.

If a file you need is outside your list, STOP BEFORE FILING and hand back the exact change: a return is filed once per start.

tasks.title: The browser install check cannot run a real command, a job's bound rests on its longest run, and a seed's failure is described as it was seen
tasks.description:
The check that runs the browser install's shell against stubs (`tools/check-browser-install.py`) landed with a review that found two mediums and four lows. The phase's findings carry each in full (read them with the brief); this is what they amount to.

1. THE CHECK CAN RUN A REAL COMMAND (medium). Its `sudo` stub execs whatever follows, PATH still ends in the host's directories, and `rm` has no stub, so a line added to the action later (`sudo rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*`, `sudo tee`, `sudo sh -c`, a tool by absolute path) would run on a developer's machine in the lint slice and under the sweep. The reviewer showed it: an appended `sudo rm -rf <outside>` deleted a file outside the fixture while the check stayed green. The property to hold is an invariant, not a longer list of stubs: NOTHING the action's shell starts may be anything but a stub or a tool on an explicit allow-list of read-only utilities, and nothing may write outside the fixture root. So: PATH is the fixture's bin directory and nothing else (the allowed real tools are linked into it by name, the list is one table in the check with a reason per entry), the `sudo` stub starts only a name it finds in that directory and otherwise prints what was refused and exits non-zero, `rm` and every other writer is a stub confined to the fixture root, stdin is closed, and a command the shell cannot find FAILS the case (an unknown command must be red, never skipped). Say in the docstring what remains outside this (a tool invoked by an absolute path in the action is not stopped by PATH: add a static case that the action's `run:` blocks name no absolute path to an executable, or state plainly that this is unguarded and why). Selftest rows, each proven red: an appended `sudo touch <outside>` and `sudo rm -rf <outside>` leave the outside untouched and turn the check red; a new unstubbed command in a step turns it red; and the allow direction: the committed action is green.

2. THE PANEL JOB'S BOUND RESTS ON A STALE FIGURE (medium). `longest browser-panel` names 7m46s while run 44424245100 has that job at 11m29s (success; `gh run view 44424245100 --json jobs`), so the bound of 18 is under the two-times rule and passes only because the stale line is the one read. Set the line from the longest green run with its id and timestamps, and the bound by the rule. Then close the class rather than the instance: the line is hand-maintained and has now been stale twice in one phase. Either the parity tool can be asked which recorded figure is the longest among runs named in the workflow's own comments and fails when a line is not the maximum of the figures beside it, or the comment keeps exactly ONE figure per job and the rule for replacing it is stated where it is written. Choose, say why, and do not add a network call to a per-run gate.

3. Lows, in the same files. (a) Actions that are plainly broken stay green (the Chromium step deleted, `npm ci` deleted, the system packages' key replaced by a constant, the `missing != ''` guard dropped, `seed` defaulting to true, the restore key changed identically in lookup and restore): assert the wiring those break, each with a mutation row, or list as unread in the docstring what you decide not to read, with the reason. (b) `gate-parity.py`'s step reader gives no runs and no problem for a flow-style step (`- { name: a, continue-on-error: true, run: ... }`), so the never-allowed-to-fail rule is bypassed by that spelling: a flow-style step item is a named problem, with a case beside the existing red case and the allow case re-proven. (c) `build_fixture` runs before the try/finally, so an exception leaks its directory into the sweep's watched TMPDIR; and on a host without POSIX sh the gate is red for a check CI never runs there: decide between a skip that says so with exit 0 and a statement in verify.sh, by what the other POSIX-only checks in verify.sh already do. (d) The documents state the failed-seed behaviour (the job stays green and a warning is written) as fact, and no run has shown it.

4. For (d), observe it rather than reword it. This is a TWO-STAGE task: hand back READY-FOR-RUN with a probe-only patch (never in your tree) that makes a dispatch on a disposable branch behave as a verified push whose install fails (hard-wire the two expressions and force the install step to fail; say exactly which lines), and what the run must show: the install step failed, the warning step ran and printed its line, the slice step did not run, the job concluded success. The orchestrator dispatches it and sends back the log lines; then the documents say what was seen, with the run id.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. Each of 1, 3a, 3b has a mutation row or case that is red when the property is broken and green on the committed tree; mutations run on scratch copies outside every checkout, restored in the same command, each confirmed landed.
2. `python3 tools/gate-parity.py`, `python3 tools/check-browser-install.py` and both selftests exit 0; the check's wall time before and after, measured twice (it runs in the per-run lint slice).
3. No document sentence describes as behaviour something no run has shown; every figure carries its run.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: the lint slice in tools/verify.sh and the CI job that runs it (ubuntu), the sweep's isolation rules for a file under tools/ (watched cwd, HOME, TMPDIR; PATH's refusing `gh`/`az`/`claude` shims come first in the sweep, so say how a PATH you replace inside your child interacts with them), `.github/sweep-costs.json` (no figure for the new file: say whether one is owed and hand back the command), gate-parity's other rules that read steps (the slice and `if` rules), CONTRIBUTING.md and the guide's paragraphs about the seed.

If a file you need is outside your list, STOP BEFORE FILING and hand back the exact change.

tasks.title: Every writer of a plan file reads behind the index lock and a lint holds the list: the two repairs re-read under it, reconcile keeps a repeat's source, and a busy or unwritable lock is said as what it is
tasks.description:
The lock change made every plan-file write of the evidence layer go through one helper under the index lock, reading behind it. An independent review of that change found the rule holds inside that one module and is neither complete nor checked outside it. The phase's findings carry each point in full (read them with the brief); this is what they amount to.

1. RECONCILE CAN DESTROY A REPEAT'S SOURCE (medium). When run A is held only as the subject's record (a clone or worktree whose ledger never had it), run B repeats A, B's row is in the ledger and its record write was refused, `--reconcile` looks for B's source among ledger rows only and overwrites A's record with B's carrying the unread marker; A is then readable nowhere and the commit binding refuses B. The record writer keeps A on the same inputs because it also looks in the record it replaces. ONE helper finds a repeat's source for every writer of a record (union of ledger rows and records, then the record being replaced), and both writers use it. Case: reconcile a repeat whose source is held only as the record; red at the branch head, green after.

2. A WRITER OUTSIDE THE HELPER BYPASSES THE RULE UNSEEN (medium). `repair-commits.py` and `repair-tests-add.py` read the whole plan before taking the lock and save every shard and the index from that earlier read under it; a record, pointer or verb's write made in between is written back out of existence (shown by a probe for the first, read for the second). Fix both: re-read inside the locked section and recompute what is written from that read. Then hold the CLASS, because this is the second time in one phase that a writer was found holding the wrong lock or reading before it: every caller of a plan save anywhere under plugins/audit/scripts/ and plugins/audit/hooks/ is found by reading the tree (the save functions are few: find them all, including the layout savers and any `json.dump` to a plan path), and each calling function must be in a table of writers shown to read behind the lock, each row with the reason and the case that proves it; a caller not in the table is red by name, and a row naming no caller is red too. Put that check where this repository keeps its tree-walking lints (read CLAUDE.md on tools/lints/ and tools/prove-gates.py: a new lint owes a row in the proving table, in both directions, and a section or line where the lints are enumerated; if any of those files is outside your list STOP BEFORE FILING and hand back the exact change). tasks.title: A malformed or hand-edited run record cannot crash a reader or pass a release: the release guard refuses when it cannot read, readers say which file and field, and a record's identity comes from where it sits
tasks.description:
The plan's record is now what every reader of a gate run reads, and the plan is a file a person or a model can edit by hand. An independent review of the change that made the record sufficient found one medium and four lows, all about what a reader does with a record that is malformed, hand-edited or carries keys it should not. The phase's findings carry each in full (read them with the brief).

1. THE RELEASE GUARD FAILS OPEN (medium). `.claude/hooks/guard-release.py` asks the run reader about merged phases; when the reader RAISES, nothing catches it, the hook exits 1 with no deny, and an exit 1 from a pre-tool hook does not block, so the release command goes ahead. A plan that parses but carries a malformed `lastRun` does it (`steps: 5` already did before the phase; `recordCut: 5` and a shared path over a list-valued field are new with the last change). Two halves, both owed:
   (a) the guard is fail-loud by this repository's own table in SECURITY.md: ANY exception while it decides is a refusal that says what could not be read, never an exit that lets the command through. Make that the shape of its entry point (one place that turns an unexpected error into a deny with the error's type and text), not a try/except around one call, and prove it with cases that feed each malformed record through the real hook on a tag command, and one that injects an error where no record is involved. Change NOTHING else in that guard: no rule, no pattern it matches, no bypass handling. If a tool or hook refuses an edit to that file, do not work around it in any way: leave the file, finish the rest, and hand the refusal back verbatim.
   (b) a mistyped field in a record cannot raise for ANY reader: `record_row`, `_cut_observations`, `resolved_shared` and whatever else walks a record check the shapes they walk, and a record that is not the shape the schema gives is reported as unreadable with its plan file and the field, through the same channel an unreadable shard already uses, so status, the panel, the report, the doctor and the binding each say "could not read" rather than crash or read it as absent. Derive the malformed shapes for the cases from the schema's own `lastRun` definition (every field given a wrong type in turn), not from the three the review happened to try.

2. Lows. (a) `record_row` passes any key of a record through, and identity is set from placement only for a task: a phase record carrying `taskId` reads as that task's run (a probe bound a task with no record to the phase's run). Identity ALWAYS comes from where the record sits; every key the record is defined not to carry is dropped before placement is applied. (b) Record-only keys (`launch`, `replacedLaunches`, `sharedUnresolved`, the unread marker) leak into the run a repeat carries when its source was read back from a record: one table of record-shaped keys that both directions exclude, with a case whose source is read back from a record (the sufficiency cases only cover keys a ledger row holds). (c) In the drive, a relaunch after a replacement starts the cancelled count at nought and is itself unbounded and uncounted, and a launch cut from the bounded list of replaced launches is waited on for ever: carry the count across (raised when the replaced run was cancelled), count replacement relaunches on the mark under the same bound and ask, and say a cut launch as that. (d) The binding refuses an unresolved share only by accident of a missing field and names the wrong cause; it refuses naming the unresolved paths. `audit-lookup.gate_banners` reads a tree-changed observation that was cut as an empty list; it says the observation was cut, with the record's basis.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. Each point has a case red at the branch head and green after; for the guard, the cases run the real hook as a process with a real payload and assert the DENY, and the allow case (a well-formed plan with nothing held) still lets the command through. Mutations on scratch copies outside every checkout, restored in the same command, each confirmed landed; the guard's allow direction is proven too (a guard that denies everything is red).
2. With a fixture plan carrying each malformed record: status, the panel's state payload, the report render, the doctor and the commit binding each exit without a traceback and name the file and field.
3. `python3 tools/bench-hooks.py --gate` stays green (the release guard is a hook; say what the catch costs, measured twice), the full sweep is green, `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` is green (SECURITY.md's fail-mode table is held to the registered hooks there: if the guard's row or wording needs to change, the file is in your list).

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: every caller of `record_row` and of `read_rows`'s `unreadablePlanFiles` channel (who reads it and who ignores it), the drive's cancelled-gate bound and its asks, `arm-release-bypass.py` (it prints the guard's own reading of open bugs and provisional phases: it must not crash on what the guard now refuses), `tools/verify.sh --release`'s early ask of the same question, SECURITY.md's fail-mode table, and the schema's description of the record's keys.

If a file you need is outside your list, STOP BEFORE FILING and hand back the exact change with the reason: a return is filed once per start.

tasks.title: A base run that is skipped, unread or still running never changes who a red is charged to: only the free resume is decided beside a running base, a late answer is refused, the own-files skip asks the runner's path, and a green keeps the base's red
tasks.description:
The change that stopped measuring a base run when it is not needed, and stopped holding a red for a base running in the background, was reviewed independently before its commit was confirmed. The review found one high, four mediums and four lows; the phase's findings carry each in full with the probe that established it (read them with the brief). The rule the earlier task promised and did not hold in every case is ONE rule, and this task makes it hold: a base run that is skipped, unread or still running never changes who a red is charged to, and never costs the task anything a held base would not have cost.

1. HIGH - only the free decision is taken beside a running base. Today the beside branch fires whenever a background base is running for the red, whatever decision it leads to. With no recorded writer session (a task written by an agent: the common shape here) or with the start's resume rounds spent, that decision is plain `gate-red`, whose `retry` spends an attempt while the base is unmeasured, and each retry is a new start that launches a SECOND base run of the same commit and is asked plain `gate-red` again, until the task is blocked for a red it did not cause. Required: the red is decided beside the base only when the decision is the resume that spends nothing; otherwise the drive holds for the base exactly as it did before (`wait-base`), and a start never launches a base run of a commit one is already running for (it joins it). State the decision table above the code (decision that would be taken x base state -> beside | hold) and prove every row.
2. MED - an answer that arrives after the base ended. Only an unanswered beside decision is dropped when the base ends; an answer given after the end and before any re-read is applied, so the writer is resumed over a red the drive already knows is the base's. Required: such an answer is refused with a sentence saying the base ended and that the decision is taken again (and the next call takes it); nothing is spent.
3. MED - the own-files skip asks the wrong path. It tests the spelling in `tests.add` at the base commit; names are matched by suffix in either direction, so a shorter spelling of a file that EXISTS at base reads as created by the task. A git failure reads as absent. A cut suite list is ignored. Required: the question is asked of the runner's own path, made repository-relative, against the base commit's tree; any answer from git other than a clean not-found means measure; a cut list means measure.
4. MED - a kept base that cannot be read back. When the steps count as measured but the reading is stale and the kept-only ask fails, the red still goes to the writer under "every red step was measured at base already". Required: it falls to measuring, or to the decision that says the base is unknown, in the refusal's own words.
5. MED - a green after a beside round loses the base's red. The base mark is settled only on a red path, so on a green the base's verdict is kept nowhere the plan holds it (the ledger row is its only trace, and ledger writes go off later in this phase), its stage never reaches the time record, and nothing tells the reviewer or the sign-off that the writer turned green a red the base commit already had. Required: a green gate whose start holds an ended base mark settles it; the base's verdict is kept in the plan; and when the base had the red, the task carries a dated note that the reviewer's brief and the sign-off read. Decide where the kept verdict lives (the task's record is the obvious place: say why if not) and what it costs in bytes, measured twice.
6. LOWS, each with its case: a base step that reached no verdict does not count as measured; the count of rounds resumed beside a base stops at the base's end; the schema's description of where kept runs sit in the cut order says what the table does without naming a position; `keep_base` handed a base of another commit refuses with its sentence and writes nothing (a mutation that accepted it survived every block).

ACCEPTANCE.
1. Every point has a case red at the branch head and green after, in both directions where a direction exists (a skip that must happen still happens: the twin cases stay green). Mutations on scratch copies outside every checkout, restored in the same command, each confirmed landed: the beside branch taken for plain `gate-red`; a second base launched while one runs; the late answer applied; the own-files question asked of the declared spelling; a git failure read as absent; the kept-only failure sent to the writer; the green path not settling the mark.
2. The orchestrator reference sits EXACTLY at its context ceiling (`python3 tools/measure-context.py --gate`): every byte you add there is a byte you cut there, and the gate stays green. The executor reference, the build guide and the changelog say which decision may be taken beside a base and what happens to a late answer; no sentence describes the beside decision as always the resume.
3. Wall time: the point of not holding was the writer's wait. Say, from this repository's recorded runs (read only, with the command that prints it, numbers in the outcome and in no document), in how many recorded reds the decision would have been the free resume (so still taken beside) and in how many the drive now holds again.
4. The drive suite is staged and long: run the blocks you touch while iterating and the three suites of the gate before filing; the full sweep once, in the background.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: every step and ask the drive prints for a base (`dispatch-base`, `wait-base`, `gate-red`, `gate-red-writer`, `gate-red-base`, `gate-red-base-unknown`) and the documents that name them; `run-test-gate.py --base-of` and `--kept-only`; the time record's base stage (queued once per measurement); the cancelled-gate bound and the replaced-launch path where they meet a base mark (the review did not check that meeting: check it and say what you found); the reviewer's brief and the sign-off for the new note; the schema's `lastRun` description and the two suites that hold its vocabulary.

If a file you need is outside your list, STOP BEFORE FILING and hand back the exact change with the reason: a return is filed once per start.

tasks.title: Every run record the recorder can write is one the published schema accepts: a record that shares its steps with the run it repeats validates, held by a case that composes each shape through the writer
tasks.description:
The recorder writes a run record its own published schema refuses, and the validator will refuse it from 4.0.0. Finding P169-R50 has the whole account. Reproduce first: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_validate_manifest.py` is red on case sp1 at the branch head, on this repository's own plan (`docs/audit/phases/P169.json`, the `lastRun` of task P169.5: a reused verdict whose `steps` are shared with `repeatedRun` and named under `sharedWithRepeated`, while the schema's `$defs.lastRun.required` lists `steps`).

THE INVARIANT, stated once and held by one case rather than fixed for this one key: every record the recorder can compose is accepted by the published schema, read by the same schema reader `validate-manifest` uses (`_json_schema`). Compose each shape THROUGH THE WRITER in a fixture (never hand-built): a measured run, a part repeat, a whole repeat, a record sharing each subtree the sharing can share, a record cut by the byte bound at every position of the cut order, a record carrying kept base runs and one carrying a settled base, one with replaced launches, a phase-scope record, and the pointer forms. Derive the list of shapes from the code's own tables (`RECORD_CUT_ORDER`, the shareable paths, the record-shaped keys) so a key added to a table is validated without anyone remembering to add a case; a table entry the case cannot compose fails the case by name.

THE DESIGN QUESTION is yours to settle with a measurement, and the outcome says which way and why:
 (a) the schema describes the stored form: `steps` may be absent exactly when `sharedWithRepeated` names it (and likewise for any other required key the sharing or the cut can remove), expressed with keywords the repository's schema reader ACTUALLY implements (read `_json_schema.py`; if a keyword is missing, adding it there is in scope with cases in its suite, and the reader must refuse a keyword it does not implement rather than skip it: check what it does today with one it does not know and say so); or
 (b) the recorder never removes a key the schema requires.
 Sharing exists because it took the widest record from about thirty thousand bytes to about fourteen thousand; (b) gives that back for every reused verdict. Measure the widest record under each, twice with a gap, with the command that prints it. `lastRun` is new in this unreleased phase, so no published contract is broken either way: say so in COMPATIBILITY terms only if you touch that document's subject (you should not need to).
 Whichever you choose: the record ALREADY in this repository's plan must validate after your change without anyone editing docs/audit/ (you may not touch it). If your design cannot make that so, STOP BEFORE FILING and hand back the repair the orchestrator would run, with the reason.

ALSO OWED.
1. What does a reader that does NOT resolve sharing see? `record_row` resolves; list every reader of `lastRun` that reads the stored form directly (the panel's state, the report, status, the doctor, the demo generator, `subject_records`, reconcile, the pointer, the group copy in the task verbs) and for each say whether it reads `steps` and what it shows when they are shared. A reader that shows "no steps" for a shared record is a defect of this class: fix it to read through the one resolver, with a case.
2. The validator's sentence promises a refusal "from 4.0.0": this release is 4.0.0. Find where that tier is decided and say, in the outcome, what else the live plan and the two committed example plans would be refused for on that day (run the strict form over each and list the lines): nothing is to be fixed beyond this task's class, the list is what the release's contract-removal task needs.

ACCEPTANCE: sp1 green on the live plan; the shape case red at the branch head for the shared-steps shape and green after; a mutation that makes the writer drop a required key the schema does not excuse turns it red, and a mutation that makes the schema excuse an absent `steps` unconditionally turns a twin red (a record with no steps and no sharing must still be refused); mutations on scratch copies outside every checkout, restored in the same command, each confirmed landed. The help payload has a byte budget (`tests/test__help.py` p5, forty thousand bytes of headroom owed and almost none left): a schema description you add is paid for by one you shorten. Full sweep green, with no exception this time.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: `validate-manifest.py` (warning tier and `--strict`), `_json_schema.py` and its suite, the schema's `lastRun` under tasks, phases and `$defs` (three places name it: say whether they are one definition), `tests/test__manifest_vocab.py` and `tests/test_gen_demo_manifest.py` (they hold the vocabulary), the demo generator's records, the committed example plan and starter template, `examples/` pins, and every direct reader listed under point 1.

If a file you need is outside your list, STOP BEFORE FILING and hand back the exact change with the reason: a return is filed once per start.

tasks.title: While the base of a red is unmeasured the drive accepts no answer that spends and charges the task nothing: one check where answers are applied, read from the table of what each answer costs, with the set-aside repair of the base decisions carried forward
tasks.description:
This task carries forward a repair that was written, reviewed and set aside, and finishes it. Read three things before designing, in this order.

1. THE CLASS. The commit that stopped holding a red for a base run measured in the background (`git log --oneline -8`, the one titled "The base is measured only when a red could predate the task") was reviewed twice. Both reviews found the same class: something the drive does while the base of a red is skipped, unread or still running changes who the red is charged to, or costs the task what a held base would not have. The phase's findings P169-R41 to R49 (first review) and R51 to R55 (second review, of the repair) carry every scenario with the probe that established it.

2. THE SAVED REPAIR. The patch file the orchestrator names in its prompt (the cancelled task P169.20-6l3 records where it is kept) is the whole earlier repair (twelve files; it applies cleanly to the branch head: `git apply --check` it, then apply it with `git apply`, which is the one write to the checkout you make without the Edit tool; every later edit goes through Edit). It was green on its own gate, proved ten mutations, and settles R42's first three shapes, R43, R44, R45, R46, R47, R48 and R49. Its decision table `BASE_TURNS` and `base_turn` are a starting point, not a constraint: the second review found that only two of its six call sites compute a pair, that the others use the table as a switch beside conditions that still decide, and that its default is dead code.

3. WHY IT WAS NOT ENOUGH (P169-R51, high). The repair limited the decision taken beside a running base to the writer decision "because its resume spends nothing", but that decision also offers `retry`, which spends an attempt over an unmeasured base. The rule was put on the NAME of the decision; the thing that spends is the ANSWER. This is the second time the same class was fixed in one place and found open in the next, so by this repository's rule the fix is now an invariant, not another row.

THE INVARIANT, to be stated once above the code and enforced in ONE place:
   While the base of a start's red is unmeasured (skipped as not needed is "measured" only by the rules of the saved repair; running, never started, killed, replaced, or kept-but-unread are all unmeasured), the drive accepts no answer that spends, whatever decision offered it, and charges nothing to the task.
 "Spends" is read from the drive's own table of what each answer costs (find it: the sentences "retry spends one", "rerun spends no attempt" come from somewhere; if the cost of an answer lives only in prose today, making it a table that both the prose and the check read is part of this task). The check sits where an answer is applied, before anything is written, and its refusal spends nothing, exits the way the drive's existing "answers nothing" refusals exit, and says which answers are open now and that the others open when the base ends. Decide and state whether the decision printed beside a base should also OMIT the answers it would refuse (it should not offer what it will refuse; but the refusal stays, since a decision can be answered late).
 The case that holds it is derived, not enumerated: for every decision the drive can print for a red (from `DECISIONS`), for every answer that decision offers, with the base in each unmeasured state, assert the attempt count and the resume-round count before and after, and that no writer or executor was dispatched by a spending answer. A decision or answer added to the tables later is covered without anyone adding a case; one the case cannot stage fails it by name.

ALSO OWED (second review).
 - R52: the own-files skip must hold only for a path the base commit's tree lacks AND that the task did not arrive at by renaming or copying a base file (ask git with rename detection); compare the way the filesystem compares (a case-insensitive filesystem holds `Tests/X.py` and `tests/x.py` as one file); a symlink measures. Each with the twin that still skips.
 - R53: a settled reading is kept and noted only against the red it was measured for; a mark that joined another start's base run is decided and keeps nothing it did not measure.
 - R54: each sentence says what the code knows (the green-over-base-red note does not name a cause it did not observe; a replaced launch is not "ended"; the joined-unread sentence; the join's line for a run that never started; the documents say WHICH starts join).
 - R55: cases for a green gate whose base mark is already decided or still running; the table total by construction rather than by a dead default; a case in the gate runner's own suite for a base step that reached no verdict.
 - The table: either every site that reads a base mark's state decides through it, or say plainly in its comment which sites decide by their own condition and why that is safe. A table that is a comment beside the code is the thing the second review caught.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. Every finding R41 to R49 and R51 to R55 has a case red at the branch head (before the patch) or, for those the patch already settles, red at the head and green with the patch; R51 to R55 red WITH the patch applied and green after your change. Say which is which.
2. Mutations on scratch copies outside every checkout, restored in the same command, each confirmed landed: the invariant's check removed; `retry` beside a base applied; the spend table saying `retry` costs nothing; a renamed file read as the task's own; a joined mark keeping a reading; plus the saved repair's ten, re-run against the final code.
3. plugins/audit/reference/orchestrator.md sits exactly at its context ceiling: `python3 tools/measure-context.py --gate` stays green, a byte added there is a byte cut there. The help payload's budget (`tests/test__help.py` p5) has almost no room: a schema description you add is paid for by one you shorten.
4. The drive suite is staged and long, and one of its cases (bq4, a base run killed while it measures) is known to fail once in a while under load: if it is the only red of a run, run its block again alone twice and report all three results rather than calling it green or red.
5. Full sweep green with no exception, after the last edit.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: every decision and step the drive prints for a red and for a base (`gate-red`, `gate-red-writer`, `gate-red-base`, `gate-red-base-unknown`, `dispatch-base`, `wait-base`) and the documents that name them or their answers; the `auto` mode's choice among answers (it must never choose one the invariant refuses: check it and say); `run-test-gate.py --base-of` and `--kept-only`; the time record's base stage (once per measurement); the cancelled-gate bound and the replaced-launch path where they meet a base mark; the reviewer's brief and the sign-off (the note's reader, in audit-lookup.py); the schema's `lastRun.baseRed` description and the suites that hold its vocabulary.

If a file you need is outside your list, STOP BEFORE FILING and hand back the exact change with the reason: a return is filed once per start.

tasks.title: A red waits for its base: the drive no longer decides a red beside a base run still measuring, so nothing is charged or decided while a base is unmeasured, by construction
tasks.description:
Three independent reviews in a row found the same class in the same feature, each time in the place the previous repair did not look: first a plain red decision answered with `retry` beside a running base (P169-R41), then `retry` on the writer decision beside it (P169-R51), then a decision produced elsewhere (the no-return ask after a resumed round) that goes past the refusal because only the red-gate decision records the key the refusal reads (P169-R59), with two more consequences of the same state (a killed base leaves the decision stuck, R60; a gate gone green before the base ends is never settled, R61). Each repair was sound for what it covered. The feature's state space (decisions x answers x who produced the decision x what the base is doing x green or red x waves) is what keeps producing the next one.

THE DECISION THIS TASK CARRIES OUT: the drive no longer decides a red beside a base run that is still measuring. A red whose base is being measured WAITS for it (`wait-base`), as it did before this phase. Then the invariant "nothing is charged to a task, and nothing about its red is decided, while the base of that red is unmeasured" holds by construction: there is no pending decision to answer, no writer round to run, no gate to turn green, while a base runs. The measured basis for giving the feature up is in the phase's records: on this repository's recorded runs the beside decision applied to no red at all (every recorded red took the agent path), and its derived saving on the session-writer path was the base run's own duration, which the same phase already cut by measuring only the red steps. The feature is not lost: it is recorded for the session-per-task design, where a task has its own tree and the writer is a session, with what these three reviews established as its entry conditions.

WHAT STAYS (all of it is on the branch head, and none of it depends on deciding beside a base): a base run is not started for a red in files the task created and the base lacks (with the rename, letter-case and symlink readings); a red whose steps a recorded or kept base run already measured reads that run; a measured base is kept on the red's record; a base step that reached no verdict is not "measured"; a start joins a base run already measuring its commit rather than launching a second; `keep_base` refuses another commit.

WHAT GOES: every path by which a decision about a red is taken, printed, answered, re-taken or settled while its base runs: the beside turn in the decision table, the rule telling the orchestrator to call next at once after `dispatch-base`, the beside mark and its end detection, the re-take of a beside decision, the count of rounds resumed beside a base and its sentence, the refusal of a late answer to a beside decision, and the green-over-running-base settle. For each of the following, decide by REACHABILITY and say which way it went and why: the settle on a green gate with its kept reading (`settledOf`), the dated note and its reader in the reviewer's brief and the sign-off (with every red held until its base is read, can a gate still go green over a base mark that is ended and undecided? if nothing reaches it, it goes, with its record key, its schema sentence and its composed record shape; if something does, it stays with a case that reaches it by that path); the refusal of a spending answer over an unmeasured base (it still has one real subject: the base-unknown decision, where the base can still be measured and `retry` is offered; keep the refusal for that, reading the START'S OWN BASE MARK in the drive's state rather than a key on the decision, so that any decision for that task, whoever produced it, is covered; a decision with no record of what its base stands on fails closed).
 Dead code is removed, not left behind a switch: no option, no flag, no table row that nothing takes.

ALSO OWED.
 - R62: the table of what an answer costs prices resume rounds as well as attempts; every rule line and every sentence that names a cost is held to it by the case that already holds the attempt wording (extend its reading rather than adding a second one); the list of answers open now applies the same session test the refusal applies.
 - R63: the own-files skip's sentence says what it knows: the failing suite is a file the task created and the base lacks; where the cases in it come from is not read. State whether measuring when the created file imports a test file the base has is worth its cost, with a count from this repository's recorded reds (read only, the command in the outcome, the number in no document); do it only if that count says so.
 - The three probes of the third review become cases: the resumed round with no result, the killed base, the gate green before the base ends. With the beside decision gone each must show there was nothing to answer or settle at that point, and each must be red at the branch head.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. A derived case: for every decision the drive can print for a task (all of `DECISIONS`, not only the red ones), staged while that task's start holds a base mark that is launched and not ended, no answer is accepted that spends (from the cost table) and none dispatches a writer or an executor; in practice the drive prints `wait-base` and no decision at all, and the case asserts that first. A decision it cannot stage in that state fails by name.
2. Mutations on scratch copies outside every checkout, restored in the same command, each confirmed landed: the hold removed for the writer decision; the hold removed for the plain red; the refusal reading a key on the decision instead of the base mark; the cost table pricing resume as free; plus the earlier repairs' mutations that still have a subject, re-run against the final code (say which no longer have one, and why).
3. plugins/audit/reference/orchestrator.md sits exactly at its context ceiling and its paragraph on the base decision changes (it says "only resume beside it"): the reworded paragraph is no longer than the one it replaces, and `python3 tools/measure-context.py --gate` stays green. The executor reference, the build guide and the changelog describe one behaviour: a red waits for its base. The changelog's Unreleased entries about the beside decision are rewritten to what ships, not appended to: a reader of the release notes must not meet a feature and its removal.
4. Bytes: a record key that goes makes the widest record no wider; measured twice with a gap, in the outcome.
5. Wall time, said honestly in the outcome: what a red now waits on this repository's recorded base durations (the commands from the earlier accounts are in the phase's returns), and that this is the same wait as before the phase minus the base runs the skip rules avoid.
6. Full sweep green with no exception, after the last edit.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: every decision and step the drive prints for a red and for a base and the documents that name them or their answers; `run-test-gate.py --base-of` and `--kept-only`; the time record's base stage (queued once per measurement: with no beside path, by which call); the join of an earlier start's base; the cancelled-gate bound and the replaced-launch path where they meet a base mark; the reviewer's brief and the sign-off if the note's reader goes; the schema's `lastRun.baseRed` description, the composed record shapes that hold every record to the schema (a key that goes leaves the tables and its shape), and the vocabulary suites.

If a file you need is outside your list, STOP BEFORE FILING and hand back the exact change with the reason: a return is filed once per start.

tasks.title: A wait for a base run has an exit the drive prints: a launch whose process cannot have been its own, or that has waited past a bound read off recorded runs, is cut short, and no sentence printed while waiting names an answer that is refused
tasks.description:
A red now waits for its base run again, and an independent review could not get anything decided or charged while it waits. What it found is the other side of that: the wait itself has no way out when the base run's process can never be read as ended, and the sentences printed meanwhile point at an answer the drive refuses. The phase's findings P169-R64 (medium) and R65 to R67 (lows) carry each with its probe; the reviewer's probes are named in the orchestrator's prompt.

THE RULE: every state the drive can wait in for a base run has an exit the drive itself prints, and every sentence printed while it waits names only what is open at that moment.

1. R64, the wait. A launch whose recorded pid reads alive holds for ever: after a pid is reused by an unrelated process, or when the pid's state cannot be read (another user's process), `wait-base` repeats with no age and no bound; `measure-base` and `block` answer that no decision is pending; the printed run line, run again, says the run already ran and to answer `measure-base`, which was just refused. Required: (a) a launch is read as cut short, and the base-unknown decision asked, when the process holding its pid started AFTER the launch was recorded (read the process's start time where the platform gives it; say what each platform gives and what happens where it gives nothing), or when the wait has passed a bound derived from the base's own recorded durations (find how the drive already decides foreground against background from a recorded mean and how gates time out, and derive from that rather than inventing a number; say the bound's basis in the sentence that announces it); (b) `wait-base` says how long it has waited and when the bound falls; (c) the already-ran refusal names something open. Do not change what a healthy wait prints beyond the age, and prove a base run that is slow but alive is NOT cut short inside its bound.
2. R65, a base that never leaves a reading. A base run that dies on every measurement stays "unknowable but measurable", so the answers that spend never open and the bound that opens them counts only bases whose code moved. Required: a base run that stopped without a reading counts toward that bound, and past it the decision says the base was never measured, by how many tries, and opens the spending answers. Also stage, through its real producer and not through stubs, the shape the review could not: a red whose record lacks the base's head while a kept base resolves (the review reads it as asking the same refused decision again after `measure-base`); it either reaches an exit or is fixed.
3. R66, the cases. A case with a follower recipe on the red asserting nothing of it runs while the drive waits (today narrowing the gate step's own hold survives every block); the reading that holds each rule line's cost words to the cost table is built from the table's own words and fails on a clause naming an answer with a cost it cannot classify (today "resume spends no session round" passes); the base-killing helper used by case bq4 goes through the one helper that waits for the drive's liveness reading (that case has cost a gate run in three phases); the build guide's case ranges are read off the suite.
4. R67, the cost table is keyed by decision and answer where one word has two costs (`resume` on the no-return ask resumes the agent and counts no round), and the documents say which resume spends a round.

ACCEPTANCE. Each point has a case red at the branch head and green after; the pid-reuse and unreadable-pid probes become cases through the drive's real liveness reading (a stub only for the clock and the process table, with the stubbed shapes taken from what the real reading returns on this platform); mutations on scratch copies outside every checkout, restored in the same command, each confirmed landed: the age bound removed; the start-time check inverted; a slow live base cut short; a stopped base not counted toward the bound; the hold in the gate step narrowed (must now go red by the follower case); a cost clause the reading cannot classify accepted. plugins/audit/reference/orchestrator.md has three bytes under its context ceiling: `python3 tools/measure-context.py --gate` stays green, and a signal or step you reword there does not grow. Full sweep green with no exception after the last edit.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: `wait-base`, `dispatch-base`, `gate-red-base-unknown` and `measure-base` and every document naming them; the sweep of base trees and the release of a base launch's claim when a wait is cut short (no tree and no claim left behind: the killed-base cases already assert this for a killed run); the join of an earlier start's base (a joined wait is cut short by the same rule); the time record's base stage for a wait that was cut short; the cancelled-gate bound, which counts a different thing and must not be merged with this one; Windows, where the pid probe is another path (say what the case covers there and hand the orchestrator the command and expected output for a run on a Windows machine if a path cannot be exercised here).

If a file you need is outside your list, STOP BEFORE FILING and hand back the exact change with the reason: a return is filed once per start.

tasks.title: The browser install check holds its confinement against every way a shell starts a program, not PATH alone, and the seed comment says only what the recorded runs show
tasks.description:
The browser install check was rebuilt so that nothing the action's shell starts can be anything but a stub or an allow-listed tool. The task's reviewer found the one place the invariant falls short (the phase's finding P169-R70, medium, with its probe) and a sentence that contradicts runs the same comment records (P169-R71, low).

1. R70. The confinement rests on PATH alone, and the shell has ways to start a program that do not consult PATH: `command -p` (it uses the system's default path: the reviewer ran `command -p touch` and `command -p ls /` under an empty PATH and the real tools ran), a command word holding a slash that is relative or built from a variable (`../../../bin/rm`, `"$X/rm"`: the static case's lookbehind excludes `.` and `$`), `exec`, a `PATH=` assignment inside the script, `env`, `hash -p`, `enable -f`, `source`/`.` of a file outside the fixture, and whatever else you find by reading the bash manual's sections on command search and on builtins that take a path (do the reading: this list is the reviewer's and mine, and the class has already been under-enumerated once). The property is the task's: NOTHING the action's shell starts may be anything but a stub or an allow-listed tool. Hold it as an invariant rather than as a longer deny-list where you can: prefer a positive rule over the script text (every command word of every `run:` line is a bare name that is a stub, an allow-listed tool, or a shell builtin on a table of builtins shown harmless, each with a reason; anything else is red by name) over refusing spellings one at a time; if a positive rule over shell text is not sound without a real parser, say exactly why, hold what can be held statically, and list the rest in the docstring as unguarded with the reason, so the docstring's "stays outside" list is true and complete. Rows, each proven red on scratch copies outside every checkout with an outside target inside your own scratch directory only: an appended `command -p rm -rf <outside>`, a relative-path and a variable-built command word, an `exec`, a `PATH=` line; and the allow direction: the committed action stays green and no row over-fires on a line the action really has.
2. R71. The comment's "Not seen: ... or a seed that saves" contradicts the two runs the same comment and CONTRIBUTING.md record as a seed that missed and saved. Say what was meant (a FAILED seed that still saves has not been seen) in every place the sentence was written.

ACCEPTANCE. Each mutation row red when the property is broken and green on the committed tree, each confirmed landed and restored in the same command; `python3 tools/check-browser-install.py` and its selftest, `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` and its selftest exit 0; the check's CPU time before and after measured twice with a gap (it runs in the per-run lint slice; its CPU roughly doubled in the task before this one, so say what this adds); the full sweep green after the last edit.

(1) By reading: run_script calls script_problems before starting any step and never runs a script the reader refuses, and new case sd8 reports the same reading for the steps the cases run. The reader is a new section, a subset shell lexer/parser that refuses any shape it does not read. Its rule is positive: every command word is a bare literal name that is a stub, a shell stub, an ALLOWED_TOOLS entry, a function the script defines, or a builtin on the new BUILTINS table, called in the shape its row allows (set only as `set --`, printf only with a single-quoted format, eval only of the apt-config stub's output, `[` only with -z/-n/-d or =/!= on double-quoted operands).
