tasks.title: A guard reports what it cannot decide: the plan merge resolver compares against a reference a person cannot move, the writers lint drops no call it cannot resolve, and a writer's row covers only the sites and the proof it names
tasks.description:
The task that put every plan writer behind the index lock and added a total lint over writers was read by two reviewers before it was committed: an independent one that tried to break it (probes named in the orchestrator's prompt) and the drive's own. Neither found a regression; both found places where the new guard claims more than it holds. The phase's findings P169-R72, R73, R74 (mediums) and R75 (lows), plus the findings the drive filed from its reviewer's return for that task, carry each in full; read them with the brief. This is what they amount to.

THE RULE FOR THE WHOLE TASK: a guard reports what it cannot decide; it never drops it. That holds for the resolver's comparison, for the lint's resolution of a call, and for what a table row is taken to cover.

1. R72, the resolver loses a staged stray write. `resolve` compares each target with "what git's merge left" by reading the index, and the person moves the index with ordinary commands: after `git add` of the shard holding a write made while the merge was stopped, resolve exits 0 and rewrites it. Required: the reference is one that nothing a person runs during a merge can move (the clean merge's own result computed from the merge's sides, or what resolve derives for that path); state above the code which reference you chose, why it cannot be moved, and what git commands you checked against it (add, add -u, stash is refused mid-merge or not, checkout of a path, restore --staged, a second resolve). Cases: the stray write staged; staged then modified again; the allow cases already in the suite stay byte-identical. The guide and the changelog say what is compared.
2. R73, the lint drops what it cannot resolve. A call to a resolved writer whose path argument cannot be located (starred, keywords, omitted for a default) is skipped: three shapes escape, one through the plugin's own atomic writer, and one already exists in the tree (a function passing a starred tuple to its undo helper). Required: an unlocatable path argument is a site of the CALLING function with the reason said; a default expression is read as the path; the existing instance gets a true row. Go through every `continue`, early return and `None` in the lint's resolution and decide each the same way: either it is shown harmless in a comment that says why, or it reports. Then the unlisted escapes of R75: a write at module level (and a forwarder whose only caller is module level), a primitive imported by bare name (`from os import replace`), and deletes or truncations of a plan file: read each or list it. The WHAT IT CANNOT SEE list must then be TRUE AND COMPLETE against the independent review's probe table (every probe either goes red by name or is on the list with the reason it is not read).
3. R74, a row covers more than it names. (a) A classified function's new write is covered by its existing row: other-writers rows carry the callee pattern as plan rows do, so a new write through another callee is red by name; the converter's row admits any bare primitive: move its backup copy into a helper with a row of its own so no row's pattern is "any write". (b) The rows of callers that go through the one locked helper (`write_plan_file`) name a case that checks line order INSIDE the helper; it passes when a caller's change function returns a document read before the lock, the defect the repairs had. Each such caller gets an interleaving case of its own through the pause-at-acquire harness the verbs' cases already use (the record writers, the pointer writer, the base keeper, the reconcile path, the phase's CI record, the held full runs, the evidence-since stamp), and the row names that case. (c) The verbs' shared case proves call position only: say so in its reason, and add one behavioural case per MECHANISM the thirty verb rows share (they already have several: name which mechanism each stands for) rather than per verb.
4. R75 and the drive reviewer's lows, in the same files: the converter's window is the whole multi-file save (seconds on a large plan): either the compare moves to just before each file is written, or the sentence says the save and the row's reason says the lock is taken by the command's document, not by the script; the unwritable-claim sentence says only what was established (no holder was looked for); a holder that dies during the wait is not worded as busy; the drive reads the busy sentence from the runner's own refusal line, not as a substring of all its output, and its case takes the text from the runner's renderer; the tests-add repair refuses when nothing is left to apply, as the commits repair does, with a case for each repair's window-miss branch; the layout command's document names resolve's refusal; settle by a probe whether the runner can record a repeat of a repeat, and either carry the chain or state that it cannot occur.

ACCEPTANCE. Each of points 1 to 3 has cases red at the branch head for the stated reason and green after; the independent review's probe shapes are cases of the lint's suite (red by name or listed); mutations on scratch copies outside every checkout, restored in the same command, each confirmed landed: the resolver's reference put back on the index; the unlocatable-argument branch dropped again; the callee pattern of other-writer rows ignored; a caller's interleaving case pointed at a pre-lock read (must be red). `python3 tools/prove-gates.py --only plan_writer` and `--list`, `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` exit 0. The lint's wall time measured twice with a gap (it was about three seconds; say what this adds). Full sweep green with no exception after the last edit.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: every row of both writer tables (a row that changes shape changes for all); the proving table's rows for the lint; gate-parity's audit rows for the two tables; the guide's rule section and its list of writes outside the rule; the driver's conflict text and the layout command, which tell a person to run resolve; both repairs' report mode, exit codes and refusal texts; the drive's handling of each exit of the gate runner.

tasks.title: A subject whose record cannot be read is never answered from an older run: reconcile, the lookup and the validator go through one newest-or-unreadable answer, the release guard refuses a plan whose structure it cannot read, and a share cannot rewrite a verdict
tasks.description:
An independent review of the malformed-records change found that making readers skip an unreadable record opened a new way to be wrong: whatever picks "the newest run of a subject" now silently answers from an OLDER run when the subject's own record is the unreadable one. One instance is a regression that turns a red into a green (finding P169-R82: reconcile); a second answers a lookup falsely (P169-R83). The same review found the release guard still reads a structurally malformed plan as "nothing held" (P169-R84), that a share can rewrite a record's verdict (P169-R85), and lows (P169-R86, R87, R88). Read each finding's text in the phase's review before designing; they carry the scenarios.

THE RULE THIS TASK ESTABLISHES (one mechanism, not one repair per instance): a subject whose own record could not be read is never answered from an older run. Build it as ONE function in the evidence module that answers, for a subject, either its newest run or "unreadable" with the record's file, subject and field; then make every place that picks a subject's newest run go through it. FIND THOSE PLACES BY A SWEEP, not from this list: every caller of the read that reduces rows to one-per-subject, takes a maximum by moment, or reads "latest". Known so far: reconcile (refuses the subject, leaves the record's bytes exactly, lists it under refused with the shared sentence; task AND phase scope); the lookup's `run latest` and its miss; the validator's phase-gate suite-gap warning (says the gap is not established while a plan record could not be read, as it does for an unreadable ledger); the newest-red-phase-row reader that derives a phase gate; the commit binding (already refuses: route it through the same function so there is one rule). For each reader you leave alone, say in the outcome why an older answer cannot come out of it. Then hold the rule: a case that derives the pickers (by what they call) and fails by name for a new one that does not go through the function, or, if that cannot be derived honestly, say so and say what the author owes.

POINTS, in this order.
1. Reconcile (P169-R82), red at the head through the real command on a fixture: a task whose newest record is a malformed red and whose ledger holds an older green. After reconcile: the shard's bytes for that record are unchanged, nothing says moved for that subject, the output names the record as the reason, the status gate's failing-tests condition still fails, exit code is the failing one. The same at phase scope. The ALLOW case: a well-formed plan reconciles exactly as before (bytes compared with the head's result on the same fixture), and a malformed record of subject A does not stop subject B's reconcile.
2. Lookup (P169-R83): `run latest` for a subject whose record is unreadable does not print an older run as the answer; a miss names the plan records that could not be read.
3. The release guard reads the plan's STRUCTURE or refuses (P169-R84). This is plan reading, not command reading: change no pattern, no reading of a command, no bypass handling. Refuse, naming the problem, when: `phases` is not a list; a phase entry is not an object; `meta` is present and not an object; a bug entry is not an object; `meta.fullGate` is present and is not what the plugin's own reader accepts (ask the plugin's reader what it accepts rather than restating it; an absent key stays "no third place" exactly as now); a phase with a recorded merge head and no usable merge moment reads as unknown, not as unmerged; a plan file holding a duplicated key is refused (decide where: the loader the guard uses, without changing what every other reader of a plan accepts unless you show nothing committed or generated has a duplicate). Derive the shapes for the cases from the schema as the malformed-record cases do, and include the allow direction for each: a well-formed plan, a plan with no fullGate, a plan with no bugs, a plan whose phases are all unmerged. Run the new reading read-only over this repository's own plan, the committed example and the starter before filing: it must refuse none of them. IF ANY TOOL, HOOK, CLASSIFIER OR SAFEGUARD REFUSES OR INTERRUPTS AN EDIT TO EITHER GUARD FILE: do not work around it in any way; leave both files as they are, finish the rest, and hand the refusal back verbatim with the intended diff as text.
4. `_deny` exits 2 whenever the reason cannot be written, the stderr write guarded too, with a case that closes stdout at exec; the arming message catches what the guard's entry point catches (P169-R86).
5. A share cannot rewrite a verdict (P169-R85): a shared path whose top key the writer never shares is a problem of the record, and so is a shared path the record also holds; one table (the writer's never-shared keys) read by the writer and by the check; a case per key through the binding, and the composed-shape cases still read every shape the writer writes.
6. Schema and reader agree (P169-R87): the carried run and each kept base run are typed as a run record in the published schema; the both-arms message names what to repair; the comment claiming agreement is true after this or goes. A case that walks the reader's checks and the schema's and fails where they differ, so the next divergence is caught at the time.
7. Documents (P169-R88): SECURITY.md's table and sentences about this guard made true against the guard as it stands after point 3 and 4, the changelog and guide say what reconcile does with an unreadable record. Quote each changed sentence before and after in the hand-back.

NOT THIS TASK: showing the sentence on the report page or in the panel (P169-R89: page sources, a later task); the wait for a base run; the writers lint and the merge resolver; the browser install check; ledger writes off.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) reconcile's two red-first cases and its allow cases as above; (2) the pickers' rule holds by a derived case; (3) every structural shape of point 3 fed to the real hook is a deny naming the problem, every allow case passes, and this repository's plan is not refused; (4) no reader prints a traceback on any shape (the readers table of the malformed-records suite still green); (5) the hook's time on a non-publishing command and on a tag command is measured before and after, twice with a gap; (6) the full sweep is green.

tasks.title: A subject whose record cannot be read has no older run to answer from, as a property of the read itself: the reuse lookup measures, a group member's unreadable red stops its landing, a run is held by the subject it measured, and one black-box case runs every command that reads runs
tasks.description:
The class "a reader answers from an OLDER run when the subject's own record cannot be read" has now been repaired by listing readers twice, and both lists were wrong: first reconcile and the lookup were missed, then, after one function was given to every reader a sweep found, an independent review found the gate's reuse lookup (finding P169-R93, high), the group member check at landing (P169-R94, high) and the report's evidence cell outside it, and showed the derived case that was meant to hold the list cannot see a reader that filters rows by hand. A third list would be the same mistake. Read P169-R93 to P169-R99 in the phase's review before designing; they carry the scenarios and the reviewer's probes are named in the brief.

THE RULE, HELD AT THE SOURCE. The property stops being "every picker asks a function" and becomes a property of what a read returns: after `read_rows`, a subject whose own record could not be read has NO row a reader can take as that subject's verdict, repeat, or newest run, and the read says so where every reader already looks. A reader written tomorrow, however it filters, then cannot answer from the older run, because the older run is not among what it was given as the subject's. Design that, and say which of these you chose and why the others are worse; the choice is yours, the property is not:
 (a) the read withholds the subject's older rows from the rows a verdict may be drawn from and returns them under a separate key for the readers that list history;
 (b) the read adds, for the unreadable record, a row placed by where the record sits (subject known, moment newest) carrying a status that can sign nothing off, so "newest" is that row for every picker;
 (c) both.
Whatever you choose, state and prove what it does to every kind of reader of rows, because absence has been read as "fine" before in this code: the evidence boundary (it must never move LATER because rows were withheld: an excuse that widens turns a gate green), counts and tallies (usage, proposals), history listings, the reuse lookup (measures instead of repeating for such a subject), the member check at landing (refuses, naming the record), the binding, reconcile, the lookup, the doctor, status and its gate conditions, the report's evidence view, the panel's payload, the drive's own decisions on a gate result (the reviewer noted `gate_went_red` drops a malformed red silently and did not trace it: trace it), sign-off, the full-run readers. If you add a status word, every table of statuses that decides (cannot sign off, trips failing-tests, the schema's enum, the vocabulary) takes it from one place and a case fails for a table that lacks it. The function added by the previous task stays as the one sentence and the one question; what changes is that correctness no longer depends on calling it.

THE CASE THAT HOLDS IT, black-box. One fixture family (a subject's newest run is red and held ONLY as its plan record; an older green of the same content is in the ledger; variants: task scope, phase scope, group member, a task whose gate falls back to its phase's, ledger absent entirely) built twice: once with the record well-formed (the oracle: what each command says about a readable red) and once malformed. Every entry point that prints or decides from runs is run as its real command over both (derive the entry points from the tree, with a table giving each its invocation and a reason for any left out, stale-checked both ways, so a command added later is red by name until it is placed). The rule asserted for each: over the malformed fixture the older run's id is never given as the subject's answer, no passing word is given for the subject, nothing is written that replaces the red with the older run, and the exit code is not the success the readable-red oracle denies. Bound its cost and say what it is, measured twice.

POINTS BEYOND THE RULE.
1. The remedy sentence names a command that MEASURES (today's advice, re-record the gate, repeats the older green through reuse); prove the remedy end to end on the fixture: follow the printed advice exactly, and the red is what gets recorded.
2. One selection of a subject's own runs, used by the binding and by the member check, so the two cannot disagree about a phase (P169-R95): kept base runs are measurements of the base commit and nobody's verdict.
3. A run is held by the subject it measured (P169-R96): a task's run on its phase's gate, held only as a record, is the task's. Decide between writing it onto the task's record and keeping who ran it on the phase's record and reading it back; show what each does to a plan written by the previous release and by earlier commits of this phase (records already on disk are read as before or better, never worse), and make the pointer line the recorder prints true. Cases with the ledger row absent, both directions (the phase is not bound by the task's green; the task's red is seen by the task's binding).
4. The release guard's residues (P169-R98): the plan is parsed once per decision; a merged phase with a null id is a structure problem; an absent `bugs` key is read as no bugs or kept as a refusal, with the reason stated in the comment and in SECURITY.md; SECURITY.md says what happens to a publishing command when this hook exceeds its timeout, from Claude Code's own documentation (if you cannot establish it from documentation you can read, say so in the hand-back and write nothing about it), with the command that measures the guard's time. Change no pattern, no reading of a command, no bypass handling. IF ANY TOOL, HOOK, CLASSIFIER OR SAFEGUARD REFUSES OR INTERRUPTS AN EDIT TO EITHER GUARD FILE: do not work around it in any way; leave both files as they are, finish the rest, hand the refusal back verbatim with the intended diff as text.
5. Documents (P169-R97): the guide and changelog sentences claiming one function is asked by every reader, and the two SECURITY.md sentences about fullGate entries and the unplaced merge, made true; the previous derived case is removed or kept beside the black-box one with its blind spots stated, not left claiming the list is complete.

NOT THIS TASK: showing the unreadable-record sentence on the report page or in the panel, and the report's evidence cell wording (P169-R99 and P169-R89: page sources); the wait for a base run; the writers lint, the merge resolver and the Windows-only reds; the browser install check; ledger writes off.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) the black-box case is red at the head for the reuse lookup, the member check and the fall-back record, by name, and green after; (2) a new command reading runs is red by name until placed, and a mutation that makes any one reader answer from the older run turns the case red without that reader being listed anywhere as a picker; (3) the boundary never moves later (a case comparing it with and without the unreadable record); (4) a plan and ledger of the previous release, and this repository's own plan, read exactly as before (rows compared), with the unreadable channel empty; (5) the guard refuses none of this repository's plan, the committed example, the starter, a fresh plan made by the add verb; its time on a tag command is not above what it was before the structure reading was added, measured twice with a gap; (6) the full sweep is green.

tasks.title: The browser install check reads a word as bash will see it, after quote removal, so a quoted option or text beside the allowed substitution cannot pass as the allowed shape
tasks.description:
The browser install check's reader judges a word by its spelling, and bash judges it by what is left after quote removal; the two differ, and each difference found so far starts a program the check promises cannot start. Two were shown on the committed check and on bash itself: a `printf` whose first word is a single-quoted `-v` is accepted as "a single-quoted format" while bash takes it as the option and evaluates the subscript of the name that follows; an `eval` whose word begins with the allowed substitution and ends with `)"` is accepted whatever sits between, and bash runs the trailing text. The third finding is the docstring that says each builtin is held to one shape.

Hold the property, not the two spellings. (1) What the reader asks of a builtin's argument, an operator, an option, a redirection target or an assignment name is asked of the value bash hands on after quote removal, in one place every rule goes through, so a rule cannot be written against the spelling again; where a word's value cannot be known by reading (it carries an expansion), the rule says so and refuses unless the row allows exactly that expansion as the whole word. (2) `eval` takes one word that is exactly one allowed substitution and nothing else. (3) A case that fails by name when a rule is spelling-shaped: every shape the refusing cases carry is run again through the quoting variants that leave bash's reading unchanged (single quotes, double quotes, adjacent quoted pieces, a backslash where the reader reads one) and must still be refused, and every shape the accepting cases carry must be read the same under those variants as bare; and for each accepted shape the case states what bash does with it by running it against the stubs, so "accepted" is a statement about bash and not about the reader. (4) For each of the two found escapes say whether the construction half can hold it too (a second hold that does not read text); if it cannot, the docstring names it as held by reading alone, as it already does for the others. (5) The docstring's list of what stays outside is restated from what the cases show, and no sentence says "one shape" where the reader allows a family.

The check runs on bash 3.2 on a developer's machine and bash 5 on the runners, and the two differ in what a builtin accepts: a sentence about bash's behaviour names the version it was seen on, and the orchestrator runs the tree on the runners before it is filed.

tasks.title: A run record merges as one value: two sides that both recorded a run conflict on the whole record, and no resolution yields a record neither side wrote
tasks.description:
The plan's merge treats a run record as an object and merges it field by field. A probe on the merge library shows the result: a red on the base, a green recorded on one side and a newer red on the other conflict only on the run id, the duration and the moment; resolving those to one side leaves that side's run id with the other side's status, so a run that was red reads back as passed, and a key only one side wrote (the task a phase-scope run was run by) survives onto the other side's run. With the ledger off the record is the only account of the run.

Hold it as a property of the merge, not of this one key. (1) A value that is one account of one event merges whole: both sides changed it means one conflict on the whole value, and every resolution is one side's value or the base's, byte for byte, never a mix. A run record and the pointer beside it are such values; find the others the plan holds (a sign-off, a review verdict, a CI record, a base-red record with its runs, a merge stamp with its head) by reading the schema, and say for each whether it is one account or a container, in one table the merge reads and a case holds to the schema, so a value added later is asked the question by name. (2) Changed on one side only is that side's value whole, as today. (3) The resolver that reads a hand-resolved file refuses a record that is neither side's nor the base's, with the path of the record, the way it refuses an answer that differs from git's. (4) A case builds the three-sided shapes (red/green/newer red; one side adds a key; one side deletes the record; both sides write the same run) and shows no resolution yields a record neither side wrote; and a real `git merge` through the installed driver on a fixture repository, not only the library call, shows the same.

Say what the merge still cannot see (a person editing a resolved record by hand after the resolver has run; a record made unreadable by the edit is the read's to report).

tasks.title: The status render and its gate give no passing word to a subject whose own run record cannot be read
tasks.description:
The status render and the status gate answer a subject's tests from the pointer the plan caches, not from the record. A phase measured green whose own record is then unreadable (a status written twice, a moment that names no moment, steps that are not a list) still reads `tests passed`, printed beside the render's own banner that run records cannot be read, and `audit-status --gate` exits 0 with GATE PASSED under the default conditions and under `--fail-on failing-tests`. The validator and the doctor warn and exit 0. A pipeline gating on the plan's state therefore stays green over a record nobody can read; only a close and a task's done refuse.

Hold it where the word is produced, so every surface gets it at once. (1) The one function that yields a subject's tests word takes the read's answer for that subject: when the subject's own newest record cannot be read the word is the unreadable one (the read's own sentence, with file and field), never the pointer's. The table, the phase head line, `--short`, `--json` and the gate all go through it; derive the list of surfaces that print a tests word from the code and make a case fail when one prints it another way. (2) `failing-tests` trips on such a subject, in its own sentence, naming the record and the remedy the read prints; `no-test-evidence` does not count it as evidence. A plan with no unreadable record renders and gates byte for byte as before (compare over this repository's plan, the example plan and the starter). (3) The JSON rollup carries the state under the key the tests word already has, as a new value; say in COMPATIBILITY.md's terms whether a new value of that word is an addition (the documents already say an unrecognised word trips nothing: check that an older reader of the JSON is not promised a closed set). (4) Cases: the three shapes for a task and for a phase, ledger on and off; the allow direction (a readable green stays `passed` and the gate passes); and the doctor's and the validator's lines stay what they are (warnings), stated in the documents as such.

The command document for status is near the help payload's ceiling: a sentence added there is paid for by one removed.

tasks.title: The plan is parsed and saved through one door that refuses a key written twice anywhere in a plan file, so no verb keeps one copy silently
tasks.description:
A plan file that writes a key twice is the shape a keep-both merge resolution leaves, and the plugin reads it with the last copy winning and saves it back with one copy, silently. The run-record reader now refuses such a record and the gate's own writer refuses to rewrite the file, but every other verb that saves the plan (`audit-task.py note`, `done`, the drive's writes, close-phase, the merge resolver's output) parses through `_manifest_io.read_json` and saves through `save_plan_json`: one unrelated `note` rewrites the shard with the copy that happened to be last, and from then the lookup, the gate's reuse and `done` answer from an older green, ledger on and off. A phase that writes `tasks` twice is read from the last copy by every reader and is never named at all. The release guard already refuses a plan with a duplicate key for itself; the plugin's own doors do not.

Hold it at the one door through which the plan is parsed and saved. (1) `_manifest_io` parses every plan file with a duplicate-key check (one function, used by `read_json`, `load_manifest`, `load_manifest_at`, the shard reads and the tip reads), and the parse returns the places a key is written twice beside the document; a save of a file read that way refuses, naming the file, the key's path and the hand step that gets out, whatever verb asked. Derive the list of plan readers and writers from the code (the writers lint already tables every function that writes a plan path) and make a case fail when one parses or saves a plan file another way. (2) What a reader does with such a plan is stated per kind: a verb that writes refuses; a read-only renderer (status, report, panel, doctor, validate) says the file and the key in its own channel and reads nothing from the copies; the run-record reader keeps its stricter rule. Remove the duplicate checks that become redundant (the run-record reader's own parse, the gate writer's refusal) in favour of the one door, keeping their cases. (3) The validator names every duplicate in a plan file, any object, both layouts. (4) The merge resolver never writes a file with a key twice (its own output is checked by the same door before it is written). (5) COMPATIBILITY.md: a plan with a key written twice was read before and is refused now; say whether that is a promise broken (it is malformed JSON by RFC 8259's "SHOULD be unique", and no released writer produced one: verify the second half by reading the released writers) and record it as what it is. Cases: the keep-both shape on a task's record, on a phase's `tasks`, on the index's `phases`, on a title, on a bug; each verb refuses to save; each renderer names it; the hand step works; and a plan with no duplicate reads and saves byte for byte as before (this repository's plan, the example, the starter).

The cost to measure: the duplicate check runs on every plan read, including the plan gate on every Edit; measure the hook before and after, twice with a gap (`python3 tools/bench-hooks.py`), and keep it inside the budget the gate holds.

tasks.title: The merge's clean-start sentence says only what merges clean, and the merge suite's recorded cost describes its new cases
tasks.description: Two findings of the drive's reviewer on P169.30 (P169-R116, P169-R117; read both in the phase's review). (1) CHANGELOG.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md say a task's start beside a re-recorded red-first proof merges clean; that holds only for a retry that moves no status. A start that moves status pending to in_progress shares `status` with the close row, so `_units` joins them into one conflict (conservative, never a mix). Decide whether the rows should let a start that moves status merge beside a close-row field the start does not touch, or whether one conflict is right because status is one account; implement the structurally correct one, make every sentence true, and add a wv27 fixture with a start that moves status showing the chosen behaviour (and red under the other). (2) .github/sweep-costs.json holds 20.0 for tests/test_merge_manifest.py; measured singly on the owner's mac on 2026-11-25 it took about 40 s after P169.30's rr1-rr10. Re-record the two merge suites' figures by the sweep's own procedure (--record-costs, or --costs-from-log from a CI log of the phase branch), never by hand-typing a number, and say which source the figures come from. (3) CI release run 45593789114 on fb4c3bfd is RED on one file: tests/test__evidence_io.py 'did not finish within 300s' in selftests (windows, cp1252 1). In the green run before it (45571636087, 5e2506f4, same suite) it took 192.2 s on that cell, 292.1 s on windows plain 2, 110.5 s on linux plain 2, while .github/sweep-costs.json records 14.6 for it; the suite grew to 576 cases in P169.28 and is not staged, so its hang detector sits at the 300 s floor. Make the suite a staged suite (its __main__ is _harness.staged_main with a STAGES table, as tests/test_audit_task.py does; read the 'blocks, not suites' comment above work_items() in tools/sweep-selftests.py and _harness's STAGES comments) so no block is near the floor on the slowest runner, and re-record the costs of every file this task touches by the sweep's procedure (--costs-from-log from that CI run's logs, or a fresh CI run of the phase branch; never a hand-typed figure). Acceptance: the case ids and the 576-case total are unchanged (compare the printed labels before and after); the sweep's own cases on staged suites stay green (tests/test_sweep_selftests.py or wherever they live); a CI run of the phase branch is green on every windows cell, which I dispatch.

tasks.title: The panel and the report give no passing word to a subject whose own run record cannot be read
tasks.description: P169.31 (d2f6e199) made the status render and its gate read a subject whose own run record cannot be read as `unreadable` through _status_facts' one tests word (evidence_row, rollup taking the read's answer). Its executor reported, and I confirmed by reading the call sites, that the other two surfaces still print the pointer's `passed`: `_panel_state.py` and both `lib.rollup` calls in `render-report.py` do not pass the read's answer, and the panel's overview reads the pointer off the composition row. Same class as P169-R110 (med), on the surfaces P169.31's file list did not hold. Hold it where the word is produced: every caller of rollup passes the read's answer (make rollup's read argument required, so a caller written tomorrow cannot omit it, and list every caller the change reached), the panel's payload and the report's evidence cell carry the unreadable word with the read's own sentence (this also closes P169-R89 and P169-R99 if their scenarios are covered: read both and say), and a case per surface fails when it prints the pointer's word for such a subject. A plan with no unreadable record renders byte for byte as before (report HTML/MD and panel payload over this repository's plan, the example and the starter). If the panel's JavaScript (scripts/ui/panel/overview.js) must change, stop before filing and say so: it is outside this list and needs the browser gate.
